articleTitle: On-Board Data Acquisition System for Spacecraft
abstract: This paper focuses on the design and development of a cost-efficient On-Board Data Acquisition System (ODAS) for spacecraft. The ODAS is indispensable for spacecraft missions, serving as the nerve center for data acquisition, communication, and control. Operating in extreme conditions, it enables real-time monitoring of vital parameters, facilitating telemetry tracking and communication with ground stations. Efficient data acquisition, processing, and transmission empower mission controllers to monitor spacecraft status, execute commands, and ensure mission success. Additionally, ODAS supports autonomous operations, crucial for executing tasks and adapting to unforeseen circumstances. Its reliability and efficiency are essential for safeguarding spacecraft assets and advancing space exploration. Current ODAS implementations for spacecraft are often costly due to their reliance on specialized components and complex designs. These high expenses pose a significant barrier to broader participation in space exploration. This work focuses on developing a cost-efficient alternative that reduces overall system costs and execution time without compromising performance. By leveraging innovative design strategies, affordable components, and streamlined processes, the proposed system significantly lowers costs while maintaining reliability and functionality.

articleTitle: Speech Enabled Writing Machine
abstract: The speech-enabled writing machine is an innovative tool poised to transform the writing process, especially for those with physical disabilities. By combining advanced components like CNC, Arduino, and Raspberry Pi with speech recognition technology, it converts spoken words into handwritten text using Python. Unlike traditional machines, it directly controls a CNC machine through Arduino, ensuring precise replication of handwriting without complex coordinate processing. Targeted primarily at students with disabilities, it aids in tasks such as assignments and exams, empowering them to participate fully in academics. The system also offers 12 styles of pre-trained handwriting fonts for a personalized experience, aiming to streamline user input and broaden accessibility.

articleTitle: Image-Driven Face Presentation Attack Detection in Biometric Systems
abstract: As biometric systems become increasingly relied on secure authentication, concerns about their susceptibility to Face Presentation Attacks (FPAs) have intensified. This paper introduces a framework for detection of image-driven FPAs in biometric systems, focusing on enhancing the security of face recognition technologies. We propose a methodology that integrates Histogram of Oriented Gradients (HOG) with deep learning techniques. This approach utilizes pretrained models and custom layers to effectively differentiate between legitimate user images and various forms of presentation attacks, including those generated by GANs, morphing techniques, and photoshop manipulations. Through extensive experimentation, we analyzed the performance of each model, offering detailed comparisons concerning accuracy, precision, and F1 score across various categories as well as overall performance of each model. Our findings imply that fusion of HOG with a fine-tuned VGG16 model can achieve significantly higher overall accuracy.

articleTitle: Design and Implementation of a Smart Pick and Place Robotized System
abstract: This paper presents an innovative Pick and Place Robotized System, aimed at facilitating product selection and dispensing processes in retail and pharmacy settings. The current challenges of labor-intensive and time-consuming processes are effectively addressed through the integration of a three-level rotating rack and a 3-DoF robotic arm. The integration of a barcode scanner and Time of flight (ToF) sensor facilitates precise product identification and positioning, while the user-friendly GUI provides a seamless interface for system control. During tests conducted in real-life situations, the developed prototype has demonstrated its ability to provide a reliable and cost-effective solution for optimizing order fulfilment processes. The successful operation of the robotized system can also be attributed through the detailed mechanical and electrical design as well as the calculations and simulations performed. Critical elements such as the design of bearings and shaft calculations, were carefully assessed to ensure optimal load-bearing capacity and the smooth mechanical operation of the system. Finite Element Analysis played a pivotal role, providing valuable insights and thereby validating the mechanical design against potential failure.

articleTitle: Advanced Decision-Making for Autonomous Vehicles Utilizing Deep Q Networks
abstract: Autonomous vehicles are poised to revolutionize the transportation industry by offering safer and more efficient navigation in dynamic environments. A critical challenge is managing interactions with other vehicles, pedestrians, and road obstacles, which complicates framing autonomous driving as a supervised learning problem. This study leverages Deep Q-Networks (DQN), a reinforcement learning technique, to control steering, throttle, and braking in autonomous vehicles. The DQN approach enables vehicles to autonomously learn and improve driving strategies, thereby enhancing their ability to navigate complex traffic scenarios effectively. Our objective is to train a model using a Deep Reinforcement Learning (DRL) algorithm, guiding the vehicle to adhere to a predetermined itinerary while adapting to real-time traffic conditions. This work emphasizes the potential of reinforcement learning for enabling continuous learning and adaptation in complex traffic scenarios, laying the groundwork for more reliable and adaptive autonomous driving systems.

articleTitle: Prevention of Boat Capsizing and Boat Maintenance
abstract: The trend of increasing inland water transport and tourism has been forcing the importance of enhancing safety measures that could prevent such incidents like boat capsizing. It introduces an innovative technique to predict capsizing dangers with the help of real-time weather conditions through a Heeling Test Simulator. The system considers such parameters like wind speed, sea rise, and visibility besides vessel-specific parameters and calculates the heeling angle and heeling moment so that dynamic and accurate stability assessments can be performedunder varied scenarios. A Random Forest classifier machine learning model improves risk estimation by processing real-time inputs. The system also has the appreciation of a chatbot aspect that allows for instant provision of safety recommendations from experiment results that could guarantee timely decisions for operators. Experimentation results establish the cutting edge of the proposed system in eliminating capsizing risks; thus, it can significantly contribute to such technological advancement. Future research will focus on enhancing predictive models and broadening the system's relevance to various categories of vessels and aquatic environments.

articleTitle: Agrovision: Smart Plant Monitoring System
abstract: Plant diseases pose a significant challenge to the sustainable production of food and agriculture on a global scale. This paper aims to develop a sophisticated system for detecting plant diseases utilizing state-of-the-art Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) techniques in corporation with Internet of Things (IoT) integration. CNN models are renowned for their precision in recognizing objects within images, making them ideal for identifying diseases in intricate leaf images. Moreover, the system incorporates IoT technology to monitor environmental factors like temperature, humidity, and soil moisture in real-time, offering crucial data for prompt decision-making. The model demonstrates exceptional performance in real-world scenarios, boasting an impressive 97 percent accuracy rate.

articleTitle: An Automated Smart Incubator System for Poultry Farms and Hatcheries
abstract: Poultry refers to the keeping and breeding of domesticated birds, such as chickens, geese, ducks, and turkeys. Spontaneous egg spawning by the chickens is viewed as a significant problem for poultry farms. Chick production may grow because of using technology to make it faster. To employ technology to hatch the eggs, a hatching incubator is implemented using the Internet of Things (IoT). During the course of around 21 days, hens manually hatch eggs. An automated spawning method will reduce the time it takes for eggs to hatch. Natural techniques of incubation were never able to keep up with modern technologies. Maintaining the ideal humidity, ventilation, and temperature is crucial for simulating the natural hen incubators. It is also crucial to regularly undulate the eggs. IoT is used to connect the incubator to a remote device, which in turn controls it. To ensure that the eggs hatch in a way that resembles natural incubation, sensors within the incubator constantly monitor the temperature, humidity, and ventilation. The results shows that the proposed model can incubate eggs in an efficient and effective manner under the threshold parameters.

articleTitle: Credit Card Fraud Detection Using GASF
abstract: Credit card fraud detection is an emerging challenging problem due to the changing techniques used by fraudsters and the large number of transactions. By evaluating the complexity and scale of fraud detection, traditional methods of fraud detection often involve manual processing, which can lead to delays in detecting and identifying new attack strategies. The GASF technique is a visualization approach that not only reduces the time required for data processing, but also provides a more visual and effective way to detect fraud. GASF has shown how transaction history pattern can be visualized effectively based on encoding the temporal relationship between transactions. The GASF approach, which focuses on understanding temporal dynamics, can significantly enhance the security of financial systems. The model performs well and shows 96 percentage of accuracy.

articleTitle: Quantum Dot Cellular Automata (QCA) for the Efficient Design of Cube Architecture With Lower Power Dissipation Compared to the Square Architecture
abstract: Cube calculations using finite-field arithmetic are crucial in cryptography and error-correcting codes. Finite fields, also known as Galois fields <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(GF(p^{n}))$</tex>, where <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$p$</tex> represents a prime number and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$n$</tex> is a positive integer, support essential operations for various applications, including elliptic curve cryptography (ECC), cryptographic Hash functions, Reed-Solomon codes, and polynomial irreducibility testing. Understanding cube computations in finite fields is crucial for developing secure and reliable digital systems. Conventional multiplication techniques for cube calculations often result in complex designs that increase power consumption and latency. To address these issues, a QCA-based cubing circuit is developed. The 2-bit cube circuit, utilizing coplanar technology, employs a three-input majority gate (MV3) and XOR gate, while a QCA-based 2-bit square circuit reduces circuit complexity. This design achieves significant reductions in cell count, size and latency compared to a 2-bit QCA-based square circuit. The power dissipation for the 2-bit cube circuit measures <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$0.991 nW$</tex>.

articleTitle: Thermal Aging Assessment of XLPE Cables Using Polarization Current Measurements & Hamon Approximation
abstract: Thermal aging is a crucial factor affecting the performance and reliability of cross-linked polyethylene (XLPE) insulated cables. This paper examine the effects of thermal aging on 11 kV XLPE cables through an accelerated thermal aging experiment combined with polarization current measurements under direct current excitation. Four XLPE cable sample were exposed to varying durations of thermal aging, and polarization current measurements were performed on them. From this data, imaginary permittivity characteristics were evaluated using the Hamon approximation to compute the degree of thermal aging. The results showed that the average imaginary permittivity of each sample, corresponding to different aging time, can be mathematically modeled using an exponential equation. This method work effectively in evaluating the thermal aging of the XLPE cable sample. Moreover, parameters such as imaginary permittivity at different frequencies were shown to be effective for evaluating the thermal aging condition over time. Therefore, this methodology can easily determine the degree of thermal aging in XLPE cables, offering insights into their long-term performance.

articleTitle: A4RSIC: Attention-Augmented Adversarial Autoencoder for Remote Sensing Image Compression
abstract: Reconstruction of images from the recent deep learning based models for image compression tasks does not necessarily corroborate with human perception and lose relevant inherent structural details. To address this, in this research work, a novel deep attention-augmented adversarial autoencoder based lossy remote sensing image compression <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(\mathbf{A}^{4}\mathbf{RSIC})$</tex> approach is proposed that achieves superior compression ratio compared to the state-of-the-art methods. The <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{A}^{4}\mathbf{RSIC}$</tex> model embeds an encoder-generator duo to generate a compact latent vector representation of the input image, which is then used to reconstruct the original image with minimal loss. The proposed model utilizes a discriminator, trained to differentiate between real and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{A}^{4}\mathbf{RSIC}$</tex> generated images using an adversarial approach, ensuring the fidelity of the reconstructed images. Furthermore, the model integrates a convolutional block attention module (CBAM) at relevant strategic points within the encoder and generator to enhance the salient features by leveraging spatial and channel-wise attention mechanism. This improves the quality of feature representation and compression performance. Experimental results demonstrate the efficacy of the proposed method compared to JPEG as well as other state-of-the-art methods.

articleTitle: Advanced Flood Risk Prediction Leveraging Geospatial Satellite Insights
abstract: Accurate flood risk prediction is critical for disaster management, particularly given the increased unpredictability of weather patterns caused by climate change. This work applies to a 1-day-ahead flood forecast model that combines geospatial data, including Landsat and Sentinel-1 SAR observations, with machine learning methods. The results show great prediction accuracy, with a correlation coefficient. Surface water conditions and soil surface moisture are both significant predictors, accounting, respectively. The model accurately anticipated inundation patterns during the peak and recession stages of the Idai flood, with results closely matching satellite-derived data. This method emphasizes the need of merging machine learning and remote sensing to provide actionable flood risk assessments, resulting in improved disaster planning and resilience methods.

articleTitle: Gamified Rehabilitation for Carpal Tunnel Syndrome: A Novel Approach
abstract: One of the most prevalent neuropathies affecting the upper limbs in the periphery is Carpal Tunnel Syndrome (CTS). The therapy management for CTS includes mainly rehabilitation and conservative surgery. The existing methods fail to address the issue completely. This paper describes the development of a therapeutic game that utilizes interactive Gameplay to target and improve hand function in individuals with CTS. Here, a pressure sensor is embedded within a rubber bulb, which serves as the input device for the Game. The pressure sensor interfaced with the microcontroller detects the pressure exerted by the user from their hand movement and the pressure values are fed to the Game software via a serial port. The Game software is designed using the PyGame tool which utilizes this data from the serial port to run the game. This exercise might be used to improve hand dexterity, strength, and coordination through gameplay mechanics which can lead to faster recovery.

articleTitle: Evaluating the Impact of Dataset Variability on Malayalam Emotion Detection System
abstract: Text emotion detection has become an increasingly important area of research, with applications ranging from sentiment analysis to enhanced human-computer interaction. The performance of emotion detection systems can, however, vary widely depending on the datasets used for training and evaluation. An emotion detection (ED) system is evaluated, comparing its performance across two datasets that differ in origin, structure, and emotional category, is presented in this paper. We employed a range of evaluation metrics, including accuracy, precision, recall, and F1-score, to analyze the system's performance. The results highlight the impact of dataset char-acteristics on the effectiveness of ED models, revealing notable differences between the two datasets. The performance of the ED system is significantly influenced by factors such as the diversity of emotions and the quality of annotations. This insight contributes to the development of more adaptable and reliable ED systems across a variety of domains. A discussion of future research directions is included at the end of the paper.

articleTitle: Empowering Agriculture with Real-Time IoT Monitoring
abstract: The paper deals with the development of Internet of Things (IoT) which is transforming our day-to-day life. The smart irrigation system developed utilizing the Arduino IDE platform, guarantees smooth Internet of Things connectivity, permitting remote monitoring and management of irrigation procedures in real time. The system continuously monitors soil and environmental parameters by integrating an Arduino UNO microcontroller with a DHT11 humidity sensor and a soil moisture sensor. The water pump is turned on by a relay module to automate irrigation when the soil moisture content falls below a set level. Furthermore, a real-time sensor data monitoring LED display is included on-site, allowing customers to examine current conditions right there at the place. Users now have the flexibility to remotely monitor and modify irrigation settings worldwide because to the Internet of Things capacity. In order to address both over- and under-irrigation, the system maximizes water utilization, automates water distribution, and effectively manages water reserves based on real-time data. This technique works well with drip, sprinkler, and surface irrigation systems. It is especially helpful in places where 2G connectivity is scarce, such poor countries. This adaptable and scalable technology increases agricultural output and functions as a vital instrument for contemporary precision agriculture across a variety of geographic regions by preserving water, cutting waste, and improving network stability. By addressing critical challenges in modern irrigation, this technology promotes water conservation, making it a valuable tool for sustainable agriculture.

articleTitle: Comparative Analysis of Deep Learning Models on GTSRB Dataset for Classifying Under-Represented Data
abstract: It is extremely difficult to address the intricacies of traffic sign recognition in driver assistance systems and self-driving cars. The creation of trustworthy and extremely accurate algorithms are essential for the broad integration of the recognition of traffic signs in various real-world contexts. However, poor traffic image quality makes this task difficult.impacted by elements like opacity, camera movement, bad weather coupled with inadequate lighting. This research aims to improve techniques for recognizing traffic signs by comparing four deep learning models' performance—Convolutional Neural Network (CNN), Vision Transformer (ViT), Swin Transformer, and Data-Efficient Image Transformer (DeiT)—on the German Traffic Sign Recognition Benchmark (GTSRB) dataset. An epoch count of minimum 10 was uniformly applied during the training phase for all models. The experimental results demonstrated that only the CNN and DeiT models were able to classify traffic signs correctly, while the ViT and Swin models failed to achieve accurate classification. This comparative analysis provides valuable insights for future research and development in the field of traffic sign recognition, emphasizing the significance of model selection in achieving optimal performance.

articleTitle: Kinematics and Trajectory Planning of a 4 DOF Below-Hip Orthosis for Optimizing Gait
abstract: The objective of the research study is to evaluate the kinematics and dynamics of a 4 Degrees of Freedom (DOF) orthopedic prototype that is designed to improve lower-limb movement. The kinematic equations for the system are derived to model the movement of the orthosis during normal walking. The optimal trajectory is determined by analyzing the kinematics within the specified constraints to ensure efficient and natural movement. Additionally, Lagrange's formulation is employed for developing the dynamic model, which facilitates a comprehensive analysis of forces and torques. The torque requirements at the hip and knee joints are computed through simulations, and the resulting plots are used to demonstrate the forces required to support different gait phases. These findings provide critical insights for the design and control of advanced orthotic devices to assist in rehabilitation and mobility enhancement.

articleTitle: Food Recognition in Computer Vision: A Review of Techniques and Future Directions
abstract: Food detection has gained considerable attention in recent years due to the growing demand for automated nutritional monitoring systems, food logging apps, and health-conscious platforms. Deep learning has emerged as the leading strategy to address the challenging task of food recognition, owing to its ability to identify complex patterns and features from images. This study provides a comprehensive overview of recent advancements in food recognition using deep learning techniques. We explore several models, including Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs), Recurrent Neural Networks (RNNs), and state-of-the-art frameworks such as YOLO and EfficientNet. Moreover, the survey highlights challenges associated with food image datasets, such as intra-class variation, occlusion, and the impact of cultural and regional diversity. Furthermore, this study discusses various strategies used for preprocessing, feature extraction, and classification in food recognition algorithms. By synthesizing previous research, we outline major trends, common methods, and unresolved challenges that can guide future developments in food recognition using deep learning.

articleTitle: Predictive Modeling of Employee Attrition Using Tree-Based Machine Learning Classifiers
abstract: Employee attrition poses considerable challenges for organizations by affecting productivity and increasing recruitment costs. This study employs tree-based machine learning classifiers to predict employee attrition, aiming to improve decision-making in human resource management. The J48 decision tree was utilized for feature selection, and several classifiers, including Hoeffding Tree, Rep Tree, J48, Random Forest, LMT, and Random Tree, were evaluated. Among these, the Random Forest classifier achieved the highest accuracy of 87.07%, demonstrating its effectiveness in modeling complex attrition patterns. The study offers insights into the application of machine learning for predicting employee attrition and provides a framework for organizations to maintain workforce stability. Future research could incorporate additional data sources and advanced methods to enhance prediction accuracy.

articleTitle: RAPID: Row-Access Pattern-Aware In-DRAM Prefetching
abstract: Modern computing systems face significant performance bottlenecks due to the widening gap between processor and memory speeds, known as the memory wall. This paper introduces RAPID (Row-Access Pattern-aware In-DRAM Prefetching), a novel hardware-based prefetching mechanism that leverages the internal architecture of DRAM to improve memory access efficiency. By analyzing row access patterns and performing intelligent prefetching within DRAM itself, RAPID significantly reduces memory access latency and improves over-all system performance. Our comprehensive evaluation shows that RAPID achieves an average speedup of 1.37x across a range of memory-intensive workloads compared to state-of-the-art prefetching techniques, with improvements in row buffer hit rates of up to 20%. These results demonstrate the potential of in-DRAM prefetching to address the memory wall challenge in modern computing systems.

articleTitle: Intelligent Traffic Signal Management System
abstract: Traffic congestion in cities poses a significant threat to the timely response of emergency vehicles such as ambulances and fire engines, leading to potentially life-threatening delays. To address this problem, this paper proposes an Intelligent Traffic Signal Management System (ITSMS) designed to identify ambulances in real-time and adjust traffic signals to prioritize their passage. The system employs an RF Transmitter along with a compass module to ensure reliable detection of emergency vehicles as they approach intersections. Once an ambulance is identified, the system dynamically adjusts traffic light pattern to create a clear path, allowing the emergency vehicle to move swiftly through congested areas. By implementing this intelligent traffic control system into the current framework, it can efficiently manage overall traffic flow while giving priority to emergency vehicles. This enhances the efficiency of emergency response operations by reducing the time taken for emergency vehicles to reach their destinations. The implementation of this Intelligent Traffic Signal Management System (ITSMS) offers balance between prioritizing emergency services and minimizing inconvenience for the general public.

articleTitle: Apple Leaf Disease Prediction Using CNN
abstract: In modern apple orchard management, prompt and precise disease identification has become crucial for maintaining crop yields and quality. Traditional disease detection methods depend on expert evaluation and visual inspection, which can be subjective and time-consuming. This research presents a novel approach utilizing Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs), a deep learning model well-known for its ability to classify images. The methodology involves collecting a wide range of apple leaf images, capturing different stages and types of diseases. These images undergo preprocessing to standardize quality before being used to train a CNN model capable of differentiating between healthy and diseased leaves. The process incorporates data augmentation, model selection, and hyperparameter optimization to enhance performance.Researchers also examine the impact of environmental factors and image quality on model accuracy, emphasizing the need to balance high precision with real-world applicability in agricultural settings. The resulting CNN model demonstrated exceptional performance, achieving 99% accuracy on the test dataset, showcasing its ability to classify apple leaf diseases with minimal errors.This method not only improves the speed and accuracy of disease detection but also provides a scalable solution for monitoring crops on a large scale. The results highlight the potential of CNNs to transform disease management in apple farming, offering an efficient tool for early detection and timely intervention. Future studies will focus on expanding the dataset to encompass a broader range of diseases and environmental variables, as well as advancing the development of more robust and accurate CNN models for enhanced disease detection and prediction.

articleTitle: Simulating Spectrum Auctions: A Reinforcement Learning Approach
abstract: Spectrum allocation is a complicated and multifaceted matter that necessitates effective methods for balancing economic efficiency, equitable distribution, and income generation. This study uses reinforcement learning approaches to replicate the Simultaneous Multiple Round Auction (SMRA) format, a widely used format for spectrum auctions. Q-Iearning and Deep Q-Iearning (DQN) are used to simulate the bidding behavior, allowing artificial agent bidders to bid based on previous actions in previous rounds of the auction and competitor behavior. The findings showcase that reinforcement learning can improve the understanding of strategic decision-making in auctions, reducing exposure risk and assuring more efficient spectrum allocations. Compared to traditional simulation methods like using random generators for the bids of the agents, the simulation of reinforcement learning-driven auctions improves the understanding of how an auction can be designed to endure both economic efficiency and allocation efficiency. This study contributes to the understanding of SMRA auction intricacies, with an emphasis on how reinforcement learning artificial bidder agents can optimize bidding strategies over time in a way that mimics actual bidders. Results mark significant progress in understanding how bidders act in simultaneous multiple-round auctions.

articleTitle: Land Use and Land Cover Change Detection of Pattanamthitta District Using Semi-Automatic Classification Method
abstract: The analysis of satellite images of the earth's surface allows the detection of both natural and human-induced spatial and temporal changes. By anticipating these changes in real time, researchers can gain a deeper understanding of land cover, environmental changes, habitat fragmentation, coastal changes, urban development, and other related phenomena. Change detection is essential for monitoring environmental transformations, assessing land use and land cover changes, tracking urbanization, deforestation and evaluating the impacts of human activities on ecosystems. The objective of the present work is to classify various Land Use and Land Cover (LULC) patterns and detect changes of various land classes in Pattanamthitta district, located in the Indian state of Kerala from the year 2016 to 2024. The analysis of changes in different land classes within the study area over the research period was done in Quantum Geographic Information System (QGIS) software using a Semi-automatic Classification Plugin (SCP) tool provided in the software. Various accuracy assessment parameters are used for analysing the performance of LULC classification. Understanding change process is crucial to future urban management and long-term sustainable development planning.

articleTitle: Agro Vision: Utilizing Drones and Deep Learning for Precise Plant Disease Detection in Horticulture Via Image Analysis
abstract: Applications of advanced techniques of deep learning (DL) transfer learning for plant disease prediction have been gaining significant momentum during the last few years, especially within agriculture, where timely diagnosis may be all-important for crop management. This study proposes a hybrid transfer learning model combining VGG-19 and ResNet-50 architectures for predicting diseases in various leaves. The deep convolutional layers with the capability to extract highly detailed features are inherited from VGG-19. In contrast, ResNet-50 uses residual learning to overcome the vanishing gradient problem and enhances feature representation. Thus, the hybrid model proposed here takes the strengths of each network architecture to build better diagnostics accuracy and robustness. The model would classify different disease states of its kind with good accuracy by using transfer learning and fine-tuning techniques over a dataset of images of plant leaves, thus providing an application that could help in the early detection of such diseases. This combination-VGG-19 and ResNet-50-would help in achieving strong feature extraction and superior performance with respect to minute symptoms of diseases, which would lead towards better agricultural practices. The proposed transfer learning techniques have been tested on plant disease datasets. It is expected that the system will be able to reach an accuracy rate of above 97%.

articleTitle: Improved Reinforcement Learning Path Planning Algorithm
abstract: The topic on coverage path planning (CPP) for multiple cooperative mobile robots using a “partition and cover” approach with Voronoi partitioning to prevent task duplication. By incorporating geodesic-distance-based and Manhattan-distance-based Voronoi generalizations, partition continuity is ensured even in the presence of obstacles, avoiding coverage gaps. The area is divided into <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{2}\mathbf{D} \ast \mathbf{2}\mathbf{D}$</tex> grids, where D represents the robot's footprint size. The proposed partitioning method eliminates coverage gaps and overlaps, as demonstrated by two single-robot CPP techniques: Boustrophedon decomposition and Spanning Tree coverage. Validation is done through simulations and experiments.

articleTitle: An Intelligent System for Prediction of Depression based on Facial Emotions and Textual Data
abstract: Globally, a significant portion of the population experiences depression or stress due to a range of factors at various stages of life. In contemporary society, the fast-paced nature of daily life contributes to the gradual development of depression, as ongoing stress accumulates over time. Artificial Intelligence based systems contribute significantly to the healthcare systems by providing timely intervention and automating the decision-making process. Deep learning-based algorithms are capable of recognizing facial expressions and identifying as well as predicting an individual's mental state. In this research article we propose a depression detection system based on deep learning. In the proposed system, a combination of facial expression and text data are used to predict whether a person is depressed or not. We utilize Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) for the extraction of features for the detection and prediction for depression. The proposed model was tested on FER dataset along with a Patient Health Questionnaire also known as PHQ-9 for the psychological analysis. With experiments our system obtained an accuracy of 92% with FER dataset.

articleTitle: Optimized Design and Performance Evaluation of a Sonic Anemometer for Precise Wind Measurement
abstract: Precise, low-power anemometry systems are vital for weather forecasting and wind energy harvesting. The most effective and efficient type of anemometer is the ultrasonic anemometer. This research develops an Arduino-based ultrasonic anemometer using the HC-SR04 sensor with reasonable accuracy. The proposed system leverages low-power Internet of Things (IoT) devices coupled with signal processing to accomplish these objectives.

articleTitle: Empowering Autism Diagnosis Analysis with Power BI Visualizations
abstract: This study explores the transformative potential of Power BI in analysing autism diagnosis data. Utilising a robust dataset, we demonstrate how Power BI's advanced visualisation capabilities can uncover critical insights and patterns that may be obscured in traditional data analysis methods. By creating interactive and dynamic dashboards, we provide a comprehensive overview of autism diagnosis trends, demographic distributions, and potential correlations with various factors. This approach not only enhances the accessibility and interpretability of complex data but also empowers healthcare professionals, researchers, and policymakers with actionable insights. The findings underscore the importance of leveraging modern data visualisation tools to facilitate a deeper understanding of autism spectrum disorder (ASD), ultimately contributing to more informed decision-making and improved outcomes for individuals affected by autism.

articleTitle: Establishing a Robust LLMOps Framework for Intelligent Automation: Strategies and Best Practices
abstract: This paper delves into the establishment of a robust LLMOps framework, crucial for intelligent automation in modern enterprises. LLMOps for intelligent automation platforms require composability and capability to use different architectures, embeddings, and Generative AI models seamlessly with domain focus. In this paper we discuss an architecture we designed for UST SmartOps, UST's Intelligent Automation platform, keeping automation at its core. Large Language Models (LLMs) have significantly advanced AI capabilities in natural language processing and understanding, but their deployment and management, integration and using them effectively for automation use cases pose unique challenges. LLMOps, similar to DevOps and MLOps, is dedicated to the operationalization of these models, addressing infrastructure, performance optimization, security, and continuous improvement. The paper outlines the strategies and best practices essential for LLMOps, emphasizing data management, model monitoring, and the integration of AI with automation to improve operational efficiency, reduce costs, and improve decision-making processes. Through systematic orches-tration of tools, processes, and infrastructure, the document aims to provide a comprehensive guide to effectively leverage LLMs within intelligent automation frameworks.

articleTitle: A Modified Convolutional Neural Network Model for Automatic Modulation Classification
abstract: In the evolving landscape of 5G/6G communication systems, modulation type detection is crucial for adaptive signal processing, ensuring efficient spectrum utilization and robust data transmission. Machine Learning (ML) and Deep Learning (DL) offer powerful solutions for automatic modulation classification (AMC), leveraging large datasets and complex models to improve accuracy and adaptability. These techniques enable systems to autonomously recognize modulation schemes such as quadrature amplitude modulation (QAM), phase shift keying (PSK), and orthogonal frequency division multiplexing (OFDM), even in challenging conditions with noise, interference, and varying channel characteristics. In this paper, a Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) model with enhanced hyper-parameters is presented. An accuracy of 90.8% is obtained from test data using the proposed model.

articleTitle: Deep Learning-Based Load Forecasting in Smart Grid
abstract: The major concern for energy management in smart grids is the uncertainty in the power supply and demand on the grid. To address the challenge of the unpredictability of demand and supply, there is a need to accurately predict power supply and demand, which helps in the quality of power, saving energy, integrating renewable source, and reducing operational costs. This paper is mainly focused on Short-Term Load Forecasting (STLF), which is the prediction of electricity load over a relatively short period. Two deep neural network architectures are proposed, one that combines the features extracted from the 1D-CNN model and Bi-LSTM models and the other that combines the features extracted from the 1DCNN and GRU models. This ensemble learning approach helps increase forecasting accuracy. On comparing the results of their performance, the combination of CNN and GRU performs better in forecasting the load with a lower Mean Absolute Error.

articleTitle: Transformer Based Classification of Closely Related Dravidian Languages in Code-Mixed Data
abstract: In recent years, code mixing, the blending of words and phrases from multiple languages within a single conversation has become increasingly common in multilingual contexts, particularly in India. This work investigates the effectiveness of transformer based models in identifying languages within code mixed data that includes English and three closely related Dravidian languages: Malayalam, Kannada, and Tamil, all written in English script. A comprehensive dataset was developed with five distinct labels: Tn-en (Tamil-English), Kn-en (Kannada-English), Ml-en (Malayalam-English), and En (English). Transformer models, including BERT, CamemBERT, mBERT, DistilBERT, and ELECTRA, were employed for classification, with CamemBERT achieving the highest validation accuracy of 97.62% due to its ability to handle morphologically rich languages effectively. The findings highlight the potential of transformer models in enhancing natural language processing (NLP) applications for code-mixed text, particularly in managing the complexities of closely related multilingual environments.

articleTitle: Designing a Bioacoustics Gun for the Prevention of Bird Attacks in Farms, Fields & Buildings
abstract: This paper presents the design and application of a bioacoustics gun aimed at preventing bird attacks in agricultural, horticultural fields, airports, and tall buildings. Bioacoustics, a field of study focusing on animal communication through sound, forms the basis of this innovative approach. A bioacoustics gun emits specific sound signals like ultrasonic signals or acoustic waves that deter birds from targeted areas. This paper describes an experiment first conducted by using a single speaker and also through an array of speakers. By employing array speakers arranged in a specific geometric configuration and providing appropriate phase delays to each speaker, the bioacoustics gun achieves precise control over sound direction and distribution, thereby enhancing its effectiveness. This humane and eco-friendly approach to bird management offers promising solutions for mitigating bird-related issues while promoting sustainable practices across various sectors. Performance metrics of the bioacoustics gun is also provided in this paper.

articleTitle: DCS Implementation of Hot Air Bag Filter Cleaning System With Controls Using Yokogawa
abstract: Dispersed Control Systems (DCS) are a vital enhancement in commercial automation enabling central control plus tracking to boost effectiveness. Lots of Indian plants still make use of analog systems. Some additionally depend on PLC-based systems. Nevertheless, DCS fostering is expanding. It incorporates plant manages right into a solitary console. This paper provides the layout coupled with application of a Hot Air Bag Filter Cleaning System making use of the Yokogawa Centum VP DCS. The system utilizes heat technology to enhance bag filter cleansing guaranteeing far better purification coupled with bit elimination. The Yokogawa Centum VP DCS offers exact control, real-time tracking as well as effective automation. Its application increases performance, decreases downtime, and also makes sure conformity with ecological requirements, establishing a requirement in automation.

articleTitle: Smoothened CNN-LSTM Hybrid Model with Spatio Temporal Attention Mechanism for River Water Level Prediction
abstract: Flooding in river basins has become increasingly frequent in the state of Kerala, particularly during the monsoon period. Several factors like prolonged rainfall, meteorological factors, topography of the surrounding region, stream flow rate etc. influence the river water levels. Predictive deep learning models can be leveraged to develop accurate and efficient flood early warning systems. Timeseries forecasting technique using deep learning models are nowadays widely used in flood forecasting. This work is an attempt to forecast the water level of Manimala river using a multivariate time series prediction approach. A Smoothened CNN-LSTM hybrid model with spatio temporal attention mechanism is developed in this work. Performance of the model is evaluated using the metrics-Root Mean Square Error(RMSE), Mean Absolute Error(MAE), R2 error, total training time and memory used for training

articleTitle: From Wrist to Ankle: Understanding IMU Sensor Placement in Human Activity Recognition
abstract: Human Activity Recognition (HAR) using Inertial Measurement Units (IMUs) is a key technology in various domains, such as fitness monitoring, rehabilitation, and healthcare. The success of HAR systems largely depends on the strategic placement of IMU sensors on the human body, as different sensor locations capture varying motion dynamics. This paper systematically investigates the impact of sensor placement on the performance of HAR systems using a range of machine learning algorithms, including Logistic Regression, Naive Bayes, Random Forest, Decision Tree, Gradient Boosting, k-nearest neighbors (KNN), and Support Vector Machines (SVM), as well as deep learning models such as Recurrent Neural Networks (RNN), Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM), and Gated Recurrent Units (GRU). Sensor positions at the wrist, waist, and ankle were evaluated for their effectiveness in recognizing diverse physical activities, including walking, standing, lying down, running, jumping, sit-ups, and dancing. The study reveals that sensor location is critical in determining classification accuracy, with certain positions being more suited for specific activities. Moreover, combining multiple sensors across different body locations enhances system robustness and overall performance. The results provide key insights into optimizing sensor placement and model selection, paving the way for more accurate and application-specific HAR systems in wearable technology.

articleTitle: Average Current Mode Control of Grid Connected Voltage Source Inverters with LCL Filter
abstract: This paper presents the average current mode control of single-phase grid-connected inverters without explicitly using an analog loop filter. The reference and the feedback inverter currents are given to a comparator instead of a subtractor. The duty cycle of the comparator output waveform is then estimated and compared against a reference duty cycle of 50% to obtain the error signal for the PI current controller. The PI controller output added with the grid voltage feed-forward term drives the PWM module to generate H-bridge switching pulses. The paper analyses the effect of using the comparator and associated logic instead of directly employing a subtractor to generate a current error signal for the control loop. The proposed method provides a robust current sensing scheme, shielding the current control loop from high-frequency common mode leakage currents and switching harmonics, and delivers grid current with a low THD of 0.83%. A scheme to further reduce the THD of the grid current by compensating for the dead-time is also investigated and the THD of the grid current could be further lowered to 0.17%.

articleTitle: Advanced Brain Tumor Classification from MRI Images with Vision and Swin Transformer Models
abstract: Brain tumors, characterized by abnormal cell growth within the brain, represent one of the most life-threatening conditions due to their potential to severely impair brain function and cause neurological complications, including death. Accurate classification of brain tumors is crucial in medical diagnosis, as misdiagnosis can lead to ineffective treatment and reduced patient survival. Magnetic Resonance Imaging (MRI) is a widely utilized non-invasive technique for acquiring high-contrast grayscale brain images commonly employed in tumor diagnosis. This study uses MRI images to evaluate the effectiveness of two pre-trained transformer-based models for brain tumour classification, specifically the Vision Transformer and Swin Transformer. The models were trained and tested on a publicly available Kaggle dataset containing 3,000 brain MRI scans. Our methodology employed the fine-tuned Vision transformer and Swin Transformer on the MRI dataset for classification. The models' performance was assessed using accuracy, precision, recall, and F1-score metrics. The Vision Transformer achieved an accuracy of 95.30%, while the Swin Transformer outperformed it with an accuracy of 98.71%. These results highlight the efficacy of transformer models in accurately identifying common brain tumors, demonstrating their potential to enhance computer-aided diagnosis and support healthcare professionals in making swift and accurate diagnostic decisions.

articleTitle: Intelligent Speed Regulation System Using CNN Based Traffic Sign Recognition with Integrated CAN Communication
abstract: The incidents of deadly traffic accidents in India is rising daily. Recent studies have shown that implementing an efficient speed control system helps to prevent or reduce traffic accidents. An intelligent-based speed regulator system integrated with CAN communication for automobiles is proposed in this study. Image categorization of traffic signs is done using the CNN model. The CNN algorithm's output is transmitted to the speed controller using the CAN communication protocol. Recent research papers have addressed speed governor systems that rely on GPS data. These approaches have several disadvantages in a nation like India where not all regions have access to rapid network coverage. These restrictions can be removed by the suggested model. With 4 convolutional layers and superior performance parameters, the CNN model for classifying traffic signs performs exceptionally well. For the deployed model, the average time taken to process each image is 0.002485 s. The CAN module's latency is in the order of microseconds, and it reduces as the data rate rises. The CNN algorithm performs better than the current models. The governor is able to function effectively and efficiently within a considerable amount of time with the aid of CNN's classifications.

articleTitle: Real-Time Facial Emotion Recognition Using Deep Learning Approach
abstract: Classifying a person's emotional states is done using facial emotion recognition. The goal is to classify each face image into one of the 7 types of facial emotions: fear, disgust, surprise, sadness, neutral, happiness, and anger. To categorize the feeling CNN is utilized, and input is obtained via a variety of grayscale images via data collection and real-time videos. Subsequently, the CNN convolution and pooling layers are used for feature extraction, while the softmax layer is employed for categorization. Some techniques used to reduce the model's overfitting issue include dropout, cluster standardization, and L2 regularization. The model we developed outperforms previous efforts in accurately predicting individual emotions in the experiments conducted on the image collection of facial expressions. Additionally, the model performs well when used to forecast each image's sentiment using real-time video data. The developed deep learning model will collaborate with advancements in neuroscience, contributing to our understanding of the brain's mechanisms for emotion recognition. This may lead to more biologically inspired models and treatments for emotion-related disorders like autism.

articleTitle: Crude Oil Price Forecasting using Multi-Feed Data: A Comparative Study
abstract: Crude oil price forecasting has a significant role in advancing the Sustainable Development Goals by enabling more informed decision-making in energy management and resource allocation. The accurate forecasting of crude oil prices is always a challenging task due to the inherently volatile nature of the price data. Additionally, the non-linearity and non-stationarity of the data make the price forecasting further complicated. In such cases, machine learning models can outperform the traditional statistical models. The machine learning models have the potential to analyse complex, non-linear, and non-stationary time series data and generate more precise forecasting results. In this work, we implemented the machine learning-based crude oil price forecasting model using multi-feed data. Along with the historic crude oil price data, we used financial markets' data and Google Trends data, which give additional information about the price fluctuations. We can analyse user sentiment information using Google Trends data, which also influences crude oil prices. We developed three forecasting models using Random Forest, XGBoost, and Linear Regression models. The comparative study reveals that the Random Forest model outperforms the other two models in terms of accuracy.

articleTitle: Harnessing Tarmac Energy: A Sustainable Solution for Green EV Charging Stations
abstract: The future of electric vehicles hinges on reliability, with range anxiety being a critical factor in consumer decision-making. In emerging countries like India, where infrastructure for EVs is still undergoing development and government incentives are pushing for a transition to sustainable options, it is crucial to adopt eco-friendly and efficient solutions. Vehicles in motion represent a vast yet underutilized source of energy. This paper explores innovative methods to harness this kinetic energy through two key technologies: piezoelectricity and vertical axis wind turbines (VAWTs). By capturing energy from vehicular motion, the aim is to create a renewable energy supply to power fast-charging EV stations, addressing both the infrastructure gap and range anxiety sustainably. To further support this, calculations and models simulating the proposed setup has been developed to assess the feasibility and efficiency of harnessing energy from mechanical stress and wind pressure. The proposed idea replicates the installation of piezoelectric strips embedded into the road surface near high-traffic junctions, along with vertical axis wind turbines (VAWTs) placed along highway medians. The goal of the project is to optimize the placement and configuration of these energy-harvesting technologies in real-world environments. Early results indicate that integrating both piezoelectric and wind turbine systems can generate substantial amount of electricity to power nearby EV charging stations.

articleTitle: An Automated Pothole Detection and Repair System for Effective Road Maintenance and Safety
abstract: The escalating demands on urban infrastructure necessitate innovative solutions to tackle the challenges posed by deteriorating road conditions. Potholes, a prevalent form of road degradation, pose safety risks and economic burdens. This paper introduces an advanced Pothole Detection and Repair System (PDRS) designed to transform the management of road infrastructure through cutting-edge technology. The proposed PDRS employs state-of-the-art laser depth sensors technologies to autonomously detect and classify potholes in real-time. A network of strategically placed smart sensors along roadways captures and analyzes depth data to identify road anomalies, facilitating rapid and accurate pothole detection. Robotic systems equipped with advanced materials and tools are deployed to repair identified potholes efficiently, reducing response time and minimizing the need for manual intervention, thereby improving overall operational efficiency and worker safety. Implementing the Pothole Detection and Repair System marks a significant shift in road maintenance practices, offering an intelligent and sustainable solution to urban infrastructure decay. By integrating cutting-edge technologies with efficient repair mechanisms, this system aims to improve road safety, reduce economic losses, and support the development of smart, resilient cities.

articleTitle: Modeling and Implementation of Reversible Logic Gates Using QCA
abstract: The main obstacles to the development of future computational circuits are shrinking transistor sizes and power dissipation. Moore's law cannot be applied to duplicate transistor density, at least not until the transistor size reaches the atomic scale. Physical limitations such as the quantum effect and the unpredictable way in which tiny currents act in this state, as well as the technological side of limitations faced in aspects such as complexity of designs and higher power consumption, might hinder the potential and future of microelectronic conventional circuit scaling. In light of this, future designs must be made capable of using alternative technologies, such as the Quantum Dot-Cellular Automata (QCA), which is a transistor-free method and shows promising results as a replacement for the current existing and widely used CMOS technology. It is an apt replacement because of its reduced size, increased speeds, immense scalability, better and improved switching frequency, and lower power consumption. In addition, when reversible logic is combined with QCA, a lot more power dissipation can be reduced, and also circuit scaling can be achieved. Today's irreversible circuits lead to the loss of information in the form of heat dissipation, limiting further advancements in circuit size reduction and complexity integration. Reversible logic technology, which does not erase information, eliminates this problem. In this paper, a general overview of QCA technology and reversible logic is described. This manuscript presents enhanced and effective configurations of various reversible logic gates utilizing QCA in accordance with optimal specifications. QCA Designer 2.0.3 has been employed for the simulation of reversible logic gates.

articleTitle: Identification of Fiber Type Proportions in Gastrocnemius Lateralis and Soleus Muscles Using Surface EMG Signals and Concentration Measure Derived From Rihaczek Distribution
abstract: Fiber type proportion influences the fatigue characteristics and force production in skeletal muscles. In this study, surface electromyography signals and concentration measure derived from Rihaczek distribution are used to identify the fiber type proportions in gastrocnemius lateralis (GL) and soleus (SOL) muscles. Signals are acquired using standard protocols until the subjects experience muscle fatigue and are processed using Rihaczek distribution. Further, a comparative study is performed to analyze the advantages of energy-based features over complexity, statistical, and spectral frequency-based features in analyzing the fiber type proportions. Features such as renyi information, spectral skewness, spectral flatness, and peak frequency are also extracted from the distributions of non-fatigue (NF) and fatigue (F) segments. Results indicate that the extracted features showed a decrease during fatigue in the signals of GL and an increase in the case of SOL, reflecting their distinct fiber composition. The highest statistical significance of p equal to 4.26E-05 and 6.47E-05 respectively is obtained using concentration measure for differentiating the signals of GL and SOL during NF and F states. The lowest significance is observed for renyi information in discriminating the signals. The energy-based features like concentration measure and spectral flatness are found highly sensitive to fiber-type variations compared to other features considered in this study. Thus, the proposed method using Rihaczek distribution is found suitable for identifying the fiber type differences among GL and SOL. This approach may be utilized for identifying the fiber typology in different skeletal muscles which finds application in sports science.

articleTitle: Soft Computing Approaches in Enhancing Healthcare Data Security Using Deep Neural Networks and Reversible Data Hiding
abstract: The rapid growth in the volume of electronic medical records (EMRs) being collected, stored, and transmitted across networks can be attributed to recent advances in medical informatics and health information technologies. Given the sensitive nature of this data, securing its transmission has become a critical concern for researchers. While conventional methods like encryption and password protection are commonly used to secure medical images with embedded data, traditional encryption and data hiding techniques often prove inadequate, leading to security vulnerabilities and inefficiencies during network transmission. To address these challenges, more robust strategies are needed to ensure both the integrity and confidentiality of patient information when shared with healthcare providers. Experimental studies on medical test images demonstrate that the proposed approach significantly outperforms existing methods, achieving a higher data embedding rate while preserving superior image quality. The findings are unique due to the combination of high data embedding capacity and enhanced security, addressing the limitations of traditional methods. Furthermore, the proposed technique minimizes image distortion, ensuring an optimal balance between security and image fidelity. This innovation has the potential to significantly improve the efficiency and security of medical data exchange in healthcare systems, providing better protection for sensitive patient information.

articleTitle: FER-Based Emotion-Informed Gender Classification
abstract: This paper introduces an innovative method for gender classification using facial images, integrating a Facial Emotion Recognition (FER) model to achieve superior accuracy. The proposed technique, termed Emotion-Informed Gender Classification (EIGC), leverages emotion-related features extracted from FER models to enhance the gender classification process. Unlike conventional deep learning models, which rely solely on facial geometry or features, EIGC incorporates emotional cues to improve classification performance. The method was rigorously tested on benchmark facial datasets, specifically the UTKFace and Kaggle gender classification datasets, where it achieved impressive accuracy rates of 97.64% and 97.54%, respectively. These results demonstrate a significant improvement, outper-forming widely used deep learning models such as CNN, AlexNet, VGG, and ResNet. The experimental evaluation underscores the robustness and effectiveness of the EIGC approach, highlighting the role of emotion-aware algorithms in enhancing gender classification accuracy. Overall, this work pushes the frontier of facial analysis and computer vision by illustrating the added value of integrating emotional features in gender classification tasks. This work opens new possibilities for emotion-informed models to be applied in other related domains of facial recognition and analysis.

articleTitle: Deep Learning for Electrical Load Forecasting in an Industry
abstract: This work proposed to develop a forecasting model to estimate the electrical load based on the load demand of an industry in Kerala. Forecasting models have the advantage of assisting electric companies in efficiently distributing their energy demand, which reduces expenses and resource usage. Demand forecasting is crucial for industries since it lowers energy use and boosts effective utilization with optimal energy distribution. In this paper, deep learning techniques namely Multivariate Long Short-Term Memory and Gated Recurrent Units (GRU) are used for forecasting the electrical load demand. Performance evaluation metrics such as RMSE and MAE are used for testing the proposed model. The GRU model showed the best performance in terms of accuracy and minimal error after testing.

articleTitle: Advanced Approach for Short-Term Load Forecasting using Dynamic Mode Decomposition with Control
abstract: Load forecasting (LF) plays a crucial role in maintaining the efficiency, stability, and reliability of power systems. Accurate LF models integrate real-time load demand data and meteorological conditions, capturing load variations across weekly trends, daily cycles, and seasonal patterns. However, the high variability and unpredictability of meteorological factors like air temperature, relative humidity, wind speed, and precipitation levels make short-term electricity demand forecasting difficult. Advanced data-driven approaches like dynamic mode decomposition with control (DMDc) and Kalman Filter are used to deal with such uncertainties. This work compares DMDc and Kalman filters by emphasizing their ability to capture weather-related load variations. The MAE and RMSE tests show that the DMDc model performs much better than the Kalman filter. The DMDc model has an MAE of 19.47 and an RMSE of 30.53, while the Kalman filter has an MAE of 32.98 and an RMSE of 46.54. The proposed Dynamic Mode Decomposition with Control (DMDc) technique integrates meteorological factors as control parameters, enhancing its ability to identify temporal fluctuations in load demand more efficiently than the Kalman filter.

articleTitle: Morphometric Analysis of Nuclei and Cytoplasm in Lung Cancer Brightfield Images for Drug Target Classification
abstract: Identifying drug target genes is essential for improving the efficacy of chemotherapeutic drugs and for personalized medicine. The drug treatments targeting cancer-causing genes result in structural and functional changes in nuclei and cytoplasm, which are manifested as morphological variations. Brightfield imaging is the most widely available technique for visualizing the morphological alterations in these organelles. In this work, brightfield images of lung cancer cells treated with drugs targeting Aurora Kinase (AURK) and Rapidly Accelerated Fibrosarcoma (RAF) genes are obtained from a public database. The morphometric features are extracted from the segmented nuclei and cytoplasm. After statistical analysis, the significant features are fed to the random forest, XGBoost, and multilayer perceptron (MLP) for the classification of drug targeting AURK and RAF genes. The obtained results show that combined morphometric features from nuclei and cytoplasm with the XGBoost algorithm achieved the maximum classification accuracy of 78.08%. It indicates the potential of morphometric features to capture the morphological changes in the cell organelles due to the drugs targeting specific cancer-causing genes.

articleTitle: Effect of Time and Frequency Windows in Analyzing the Muscle Typology of Adductor Pollicis and Triceps Brachii Muscles Using Surface EMG Signals and Smoothed Pseudo-Wigner-Ville Distribution
abstract: The selection of time and frequency windows is having a significant impact on the time-frequency (TF) resolution and interference suppression of smoothed pseudo-Wigner-Ville distribution (SPWVD). In this study, the effect of time and frequency windows in demonstrating the fiber type differences among adductor pollicis (AP) and triceps brachii (TB) muscles is investigated using surface electromyography signals and SPWVD-derived features. The first and last two seconds of the pre-processed signals are considered non-fatigue (NF) and fatigue (FT) segments, respectively. The median frequency (MDF) and mean power of the TF spectrum (MPS) are extracted from the obtained spectra. The statistical significance of SPWVD-derived features in differentiating the signals of AP and TB during NF and FT states are evaluated for different time and frequency windows, using the Mann-Whitney test. Results indicate that the frequency-based feature showed greater statistical significance compared to the energy-based feature for all the different time and frequency window lengths taken. MDF is found to decrease for both muscles, whereas MPS increases for TB and decreases in the case of AP. The highest significant value of 5.39E-27 is observed for MDF with time and frequency window length of 201 and 2001, respectively, for differentiating the signals during the fatigue state. Moreover, all the extracted features showed high statistical significance with p<0.001 in discriminating the signals irrespective of the various window lengths considered in this study. This reflects the effectiveness of SPWVD-derived features in highlighting the fiber type variations in muscles. The proposed study can be used to investigate the fiber type proportion in various skeletal muscles under different myoneural conditions.

articleTitle: Optimizing Discharge Management Through Lean Process Capability Improvement Using DMAIC
abstract: Efficient discharge management is vital for enhancing patient satisfaction and operational performance in hospitals. This study, which adopted a case-based methodology in a leading private hospital in South India, focused on optimizing the discharge process for ESI, ECHS, TPA, and cash patients using the DMAIC framework, Value Stream Mapping, and Process Capability Analysis. Key delays in pharmacy operations, billing, and departmental clearances were identified as bottlenecks caused by communication gaps, understaffing, and inefficient workflows. Interventions such as AI-driven staffing, cloud-based Electronic Health Records, robotic process automation for approvals, and automated billing systems significantly reduced discharge times in the hospital. The findings demonstrate the effectiveness of Lean Six Sigma tools in streamlining hospital workflows and improving patient outcomes.

articleTitle: Soothing Relief for Menstrual Cramps: A Period Massager with Heat Therapy and Aromatherapy
abstract: Period cramps can significantly impact quality of life, demanding effective and accessible pain management solutions. This innovative abdominal massager offers a holistic approach to period cramp relief by combining heat therapy, massage therapy and aromatherapy. The device delivers soothing heat to the abdominal area, relaxing uterine muscles and improving blood circulation to alleviate cramping. Gentle massage provides further pain relief by easing muscle tension and promoting endorphin release. Additionally, the integration of aromatherapy with calming scents like lavender and chamomile enhances relaxation and reduces stress often associated with menstrual discomfort. This multi-modal approach provides a natural, drugfree solution for period pain, empowering individuals to manage their discomfort and regain control over their well-being.

articleTitle: Cyber-Physical Modeling and Simulation of Four-Axis Articulated Robot
abstract: This paper presents the physical component modeling and simulation of a five degree of freedom articulated robot arm. Robots are used extensively in manufacturing and field like mines, space, military, medicine, hospital and agriculture. The articulated serial link manipulator act as robotic arm similar to a human arm. The robot arm end point trajectory in Cartesian space is realised by forward kinematic and inverse kinematic based on analytical solution method and the results are verified. A simple analytical method is formulated to solve analytically difficult inverse kinematic problem. The physical robot system modeling is accompanied by a control system to meet the sequence of movements by position controllers. The controller including PID and a single board computer imitating Ardinio.

articleTitle: IoT-Based Real Time Patient Health and Medical IV Monitoring System
abstract: Current hospital practices for monitor ing patients throughout the day can be grueling, for nurses and doctors. Their busy schedules make it difficult to maintain close observation of every panent, potentially leading to critical situations. Accurate and timely medical care is essential, particularly when dealing with intravenous (IV) fluids. Improper monitoring of IV drip systems can cause serious complications like backflow of fluids or blood loss. And it is very essential to continuous monitoring of vital signs for early detection of potential problems. To address these challenges and alleviate the workload on medical staff, we propose the development of an Automated System for patient's vitals monitoring and IV administered. with the help of IoT. This system would automate the monitoring process, freeing up valuable time for nurses and doctors while ensuring the proper function of IV drips,alerting the authorities upon variation from normal parameters and ultimately improving patient safety.

articleTitle: Channel Estimation in V2V Communication
abstract: Vehicle to Everything Communication using mm Wave, Multiple Input Multiple Output [MIMO] Channel estimation is very difficult. In MIMO, channel knowledge is very much essential for correct Transmitter/Receiver combining. There are two types of channel estimation methods: Parametric and Non parametric Channel estimation methods. Parametric method of channel estimation is preferred in practical cases but it provides a limited performance of specific channel models. So to give more performance Algebraic Low Rank [LR] method is used. While single path fading amplitudes are expected to fluctuate in accordance with Doppler Spectrum, LR operates on numerous pilot sequences transmitted by single user equipment gathered by a fixed base station, where each pilot transmission shares the same DoAs, DoDs, and delays. In order to filter new pilot signals and obtain an estimate of the LR Channel, the ensemble of received pilot sequences is utilized to compute the spatial and temporal modes of the MIMO channel. The stationarity of space-time channel Eigen modes is the only need for LR.

articleTitle: Domain Agnostic Agentic AI: Enabling Autonomous Automation with SmartGenie CoPilot
abstract: Generative AI and Agentic AI systems are revolutionizing the way organizations approach automation by enabling machines to autonomously perform complex tasks that traditionally required human intervention. These systems leverage large language models (LLMs) to process vast amounts of information, interpret complex workflows, and make decisions in real-time. Agentic AI frameworks, in particular, offer a new level of intelligence, allowing for dynamic, context-aware task execution across various industries. By integrating such advanced AI capabilities, businesses can automate decision-making processes and achieve unprecedented levels of efficiency and accuracy in handling routine and sophisticated tasks alike. This paper introduces SmartGenie, an Agentic AI CoPilot developed as part of the SmartOps intelligent automation platform. SmartGenie utilizes an LLM-based framework that is adaptable and easily integrated with autonomous automation scenarios. We present a use case where SmartGenie automates the handling of employee service requests for a financial client, autonomously responding to and resolving issues. This implementation resulted in significant improvements in request completion times, enhanced accuracy, and overall operational efficiency. These findings demonstrate the transformative potential of SmartGenie to drive quality and performance improvements in business-critical processes through the use of Agentic LLMs.

articleTitle: Smart Agriculture: A Crop Monitoring System to Empower Agricultural Field Using IOT
abstract: Agriculture has long been the cornerstone of India's economy and way of life, contributing significantly to the nation's GDP and employment. With a diverse range of crops and climatic conditions, India's agricultural sector is both vast and complex, demanding innovative approaches to meet the growing needs of its population. The sector faces numerous challenges, including climate variability, soil degradation, water scarcity, and pest infestations, which impact productivity and sustainability. In response to these challenges, modern agricultural system in India increasingly focuses on integrating technology to enhance efficacy and eco-friendly. One such initiative is the development of smart agricultural systems that leverage advanced technologies. This paper presents an advanced Internet of Things (IoT) based crop monitoring system designed to enhance agricultural efficacy and conciliatory. The system integrates multiple sensors to monitor critical environmental parameters, including pH levels, soil properties, and temperature. By continuously measuring these variables, the system provides real-time data to optimize crop health and growth conditions. Additionally, the paper incorporates pest control mechanisms, leveraging IoT technology to detect and manage pest populations effectively. This comprehensive approach not only ensures the optimal condition for crops but also minimizes the need for manual intervention and reduces the reliance on chemical treatments. The data collected through this system is analysed and visualized through a user-friendly interface, offering farmers actionable insights and enabling timely decision-making. The integration of these technologies aims to promote sustainable agricultural practices, improve crop yield, and reduce environmental impact, demonstrating the potential of IoT in modernizing agricultural operations.

articleTitle: A Comprehensive Review on Lunar Crater Detection using Image Processing
abstract: This review investigates the application of machine learning techniques, particularly the YOLO algorithm, and proposes a better alternative to the existing models for automated lunar crater detection. It addresses the challenges associated with manual identification methods, including the presence of overlapping features and the management of extensive data volumes. Additionally, the paper examines the development of a web-based application designed for lunar surface analysis. The review synthesizes current advancements in image processing techniques for crater detection, highlighting potential enhancements in efficiency and accuracy for lunar geological studies.

articleTitle: Cloaked Cryptography: Attribute-Driven Privacy Preservation
abstract: The Cloaked Cryptography is a novel Attribute-Based Encryption (ABE) system designed to enhance security and privacy in IoT data interactions on cloud platforms. This system emphasizes data confidentiality and privacy through encryption prior to cloud storage and features a multi-authority ABE scheme to enable secure data sharing and stringent access control, suitable for the dynamic and resource-constrained scenarios often encountered in IoT environments. The architecture incorporates several key entities: the data owner, data user, attribute authority, cloud server, and auditor. The attribute authority generates system parameters and distributes credentials, while the data owner encrypts and sends data to the cloud. Data users with matching attributes can decrypt the data according to specific access structures. In cases of potential credential leaks, an auditor investigates and reports findings, ensuring accountability. Cloaked Cryptography aims to deliver a robust, efficient, and accountable access control framework for CloudIoT platforms, tackling significant challenges insecuring IoT data and authenticating users.

articleTitle: Securing Diabetic Prediction with Federated Learning and Homomorphic Encryption
abstract: The rising worldwide impact of diabetes emphasizes the need for precise and personalized prediction models. However, the ethical and legal challenges associated with handling sensitive healthcare data necessitate innovative solutions that balance predictive accuracy with individual privacy.
