This research investigates the novel integration of two cutting-edge technologies, Federated Learning (FL) and Homomorphic Encryption (HE), to advance field of diabetic prediction while prioritizing data privacy. In this study, we give a detailed exploration of the Federated Learning and Homomorphic Encryption framework for diabetic prediction. We discuss the technical implementation, evaluate the system's predictive performance, and assess its ability to protect sensitive patient information. Our experiments reveal that the proposed approach achieves good prediction accuracy while preserving individual privacy, thereby offering a promising avenue for the development of secure and collaborative diabetic prediction models.

articleTitle: Bridging the Gap for Non-Programmers with No-Code ML Solutions
abstract: This paper presents ‘No-Code ML’, a web-based platform designed to democratize access to machine learning (ML) technologies for non-programmers. Traditional ML development often requires significant programming expertise, limiting its accessibility to a broader audience. However, with the emergence of no-code ML platforms, individuals without coding backgrounds can now leverage the power of ML algorithms for various applications. No Code ML bridges this gap by offering an intuitive interface and a diverse set of ML tools, enabling users to build, deploy, and manage ML models without writing a single line of code. By highlighting the capabilities and benefits of No-Code ML, this paper contributes to the ongoing discourse on democratizing ML and empowers a wider audience to harness the transformative potential of artificial intelligence.

articleTitle: Hybrid Recipe Recommendation System Using KNN and Collaborative Filtering Techniques
abstract: Discovering the perfect recipe or ingredient combination can be a challenge given the vast array of culinary options. Our Recipe Recommendation System addresses this by combining K-Nearest Neighbors (KNN) and collaborative filtering to offer highly personalized and accurate recipe suggestions. Using a rich dataset of recipes, ingredients, and user reviews, the system identifies similar dishes based on ingredient profiles and user preferences. KNN leverages TF-IDF vectorization and cosine similarity to find related recipes, while collaborative filtering uses Non-Negative Matrix Factorization (NMF) to analyze user behaviour and suggest personalized options. Experimental results show that the system effectively delivers diverse and relevant recommendations, enhancing the user's culinary journey.

articleTitle: Leveraging AI & ML for Effective Bidding in Centralized E-Marketplaces
abstract: The rapid advancement of electronic marketplaces has highlighted the necessity for more sophisticated and efficient bidding tactics. This research delves into the ways in which Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Machine Learning (ML) technologies can enhance the bidding procedures in centralized electronic marketplaces. Through the utilization of AI and ML, our goal is to create intelligent bidding systems capable of predicting optimal bid values, adjusting to real-time market dynamics, and enhancing overall bidding efficiency. This research examines existing bidding frameworks, identifies primary challenges, and implements advanced algorithms to tackle these issues. Initial findings suggest a notable enhancement in bid accuracy and market adaptability. On top of that, the infusion of AI and ML in bid systems reassures operational efficiency which is beneficial to buyers and sellers alike in electronic markets. The study contributes to the knowledge base on the optimization of electronic platforms as well as presents prompt advice for policy-makers, market administrators, and platform operators. These technologies can lead to the creation of not only more efficient but also more flexible and hence more competitive marketplaces, which will also have a positive effect on the participating buyers and sellers. The suggested AI and ML-based systems utilize both the historical data and the market trends to prognosticate the future behavior of the market. These types of adaptive strategies can dynamically adjust to market conditions and thereby keep in line with the competition in the market. This study adds to the expanding knowledge base on optimizing e-marketplaces and offers practical insights for policymakers and marketplace administrators.

articleTitle: Accident Detection and Reporting System for Powered Two-Wheelers Using Internet of Things and Edge AI augmented with MCUSUM features
abstract: According to data provided by the Ministry of Road Transport and Highways (MORTH), Government of India, about 1.68 lakh people have lost their lives in accidents and nearly 4.4 lakh people have suffered injuries [1]. The number of accidents has increased by approximately 12% year on year. The data also show that people affected by accidents are likely to be in the age group of 15 to 49 years. This age group is virtually the pillar that supports the nation's development. Therefore, road fatalities can indirectly influence the nations development. In this work, we have implemented a system aimed towards powered two-wheelers (PTWs) that detects accidents and sends an SOS signal to a preconfigured contact. The system, upon detecting an accident/critical event, can attempt to convey the SOS signal in multiple modalities for redundancy. The SOS signal includes the last known GNSS coordinates of the vehicle to be able to pinpoint the location of the incident. The system also has a manual SOS trigger option that can be used as a panic button. Detection is performed by a Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) based classifier running on the system using Edge AI capability that uses sensory output from an inertial measurement unit (IMU) and its derivative data for input features. In this work, we have experimented with the possibility of improving the classification performance of the classifier by augmenting the input feature set with Multivariate Cumulative Summation (MCUSUM) [2] control chart statistic of the IMU data. The results show that this technique can give marked improvements in the overall accuracy of the classification system.

articleTitle: An IoT-Based Robotic Irrigation System for Optimal Water Management
abstract: This paper presents the design, implementation, and testing of an autonomous smart irrigation robot. The main aim is to optimize water use in agriculture through innovative integration of the Internet of Things (IoT) technology and renewable energy sources. The robot's architecture is composed of sensors, autonomous navigation, and remote data management systems, all powered by a solar-charged battery. In field tests, the robot displayed a high level of sensor accuracy, satisfactory navigation, and reliable data transfer to the cloud. Challenges such as environmental resilience, energy optimization, data transmission, and system durability were identified and addressed, paving the way for further refinement. Future iterations of the project will focus on incorporating predictive analytics for dynamic irrigation scheduling, enhancing user experience through interface personalization, achieving autonomous operational decision-making, and ensuring scalability for diverse agricultural contexts.

articleTitle: Refining Sorghum Weed Classification with Dimension Reduction Techniques in Machine Learning
abstract: This paper explores the refinement of sorghum weed classification by applying dimension-reduction techniques in machine learning. Utilizing a comprehensive dataset of sorghum weed types, the study aims to enhance classification accuracy by integrating machine learning models with dimensionality reduction methods. Various algorithms are employed to assess model performance, including Logistic Regression, Support Vector Machines, Decision Trees, and Random Forests. In parallel, dimension reduction techniques such as Principal Component Analysis (PCA), Linear Discriminant Analysis (LDA), t-distributed Stochastic Neighbor Embedding (t-SNE), and Uniform Manifold Approximation and Projection (UMAP) are applied to determine their impact on classification outcomes. The results highlight that LDA significantly enhances decision tree performance, leading to a 16.92% improvement in accuracy. This research highlights the potential of combining machine learning and dimensionality reduction to improve the precision of weed classification, ultimately contributing to more effective agricultural management and weed control strategies.

articleTitle: Affine Frequency Division Multiplexing with Quadrature Index Modulation
abstract: Affine frequency division multiplexing (AFDM) is an emerging multicarrier technique utilizing chirp signals, specifically designed for high-mobility communication scenarios, and it can achieve full diversity. Recently, AFDM with index modulation (AFDM-IM) has been introduced, offering improved bit error rate (BER) performance compared to traditional AFDM systems. In this paper, we propose a novel transmission scheme called AFDM with quadrature index modulation (AFDM-QIM), which enhances the spectral efficiency of AFDM-IM by embedding additional information bits in the subcarrier indices of the AFDM subblock, utilizing both in-phase and quadrature components. A theoretical analysis of the BER performance of AFDM-QIM is provided, along with simulation results. These results demon-strate superior performance of AFDM-QIM over traditional AFDM-IM. This novel approach provides a promising pathway for the development of resilient and efficient communication systems in future high-mobility scenarios.

articleTitle: Automated 3D Lung Segmentation in Chest Scans Using Channel Attention Hybrid Dilated Convolution-Based U-Net Model
abstract: Accurate lung segmentation from 3D chest scans is a difficult problem due to the lung volume shape variations and less contrast between the lung and the neighbouring tissues. Traditional methods are computationally expensive and often result in false positives. Therefore, this paper develops a computationally efficient and robust 3D lung segmentation approach called Channel Attention Hybrid Dilated Convolution-based U-Net (CAHDC-UNET) model. This model is formulated by including Channel Attention and Hybrid Dilated Convolution in the U-Net architecture to increase deep semantic features' learning and segmentation efficiency. Initially, the pre-processing of the 3D scans is performed to extract the coarse lung contours, and then, the refinement is done using the CAHDC-UNET to obtain refined lung coarse segmentation. Experiments are conducted on a publically available COVID-19 database that contains 750 chest computed tomography (CT) scans. The CAHDC-UNET model attained better results with an accuracy of 99.8% and BF of 99.5% and provides reliable 3D lung segmentation that can be utilized as a clinical diagnosis tool to help doctors deliver precise additional estimations.

articleTitle: Comparative Analysis of Machine Learning Methods in Climate Data Extraction and Forecasting
abstract: Climate forecasting plays a critical role in understanding and mitigating the impacts of climate change. Advances in machine learning (ML) have significantly enhanced the accuracy of climate projections, particularly when dealing with large and complex datasets derived from regional climate models (RCMs) and global climate models (GCMs). This study investigates the application of various ML techniques for predicting precipitation based on temperature data extracted from climate datasets. We evaluate a range of regression models, including linear models and advanced ensemble methods such as Gradient Boosting and XGBoost, along with deep learning approaches like Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs). Through a rigorous evaluation of these models, we focus on their performance as measured by Mean Squared Error (MSE) to identify the most effective techniques for capturing the intricate relationships within climate data. By analyzing existing studies and performance metrics, we aim to provide insights into the capabilities and limitations of these ML models in improving climate predictions. Furthermore, this research highlights the need for incorporating additional climate variables and optimizing model configurations to enhance predictive accuracy in climate forecasting.

articleTitle: Travel Mate: A Comprehensive Travel Assistance Platform
abstract: This paper discusses the design of a mobile app developed using Flutter in Android Studio, delivering individualized journey plans based on user preferences and real-time data. It combines Google Maps to investigate travel trends and suggest best routes, including flights, trains, and local transit. The software also suggests meals using data from Swiggy and Zomato, has a budget management option for tracking expenditure, and securely keeps vital travel papers. Real-time weather forecasts help users plan better, and the app gives ongoing recommendations for food, entertainment, and local events during the trip. This paper covers the suggested method, implementation, and functionality of the app.

articleTitle: Enhanced Time-Frequency Analysis of Power Quality Disturbances Using Fourier Synchro-Squeezing Transform
abstract: Power quality disturbances (PQD) critically impact the stability and performance of electrical equipment, necessitating their timely detection and thorough investigation. High resolution time-frequency analysis methods are essential for visualizing and recognizing non-stationary waveforms in power quality (PQ) disturbance signals. The Fourier Synchro-Squeezing Transform (FSST) is suggested as a better way to characterize and identify advanced time-frequency PQD techniques in this study. It is shown that FSST can provide accurate and detailed time-frequency representations of PQ disturbance signals, showing how well it works to improve the accuracy of PQD analysis and detection accuracy. In addition to presenting the merits of FSST, a comparative study with other state-of-the-art methods, such as the Stockwell Transform (ST) and Hilbert-Huang Transform (HHT), is conducted. This comparison shows that FSST is better in terms of resolution and ease of use, especially when dealing with complex, non-stationary signals common during power quality problems. The study examines various PQ disturbance signals, including voltage sags, swells, transients, and harmonic distortions, analyzed using FSST.

articleTitle: A Research Framework for Energy Efficient Distributed Flow Shop Scheduling in Intelligent Production Systems
abstract: In intelligent production scheduling, advanced algorithms are employed to develop optimal production schedules for the shop floor. Industries all over the world are now adopting various energy conservation policies due to the rapid depletion of energy sources. Energy efficient scheduling has emerged as an economical tool to conserve energy in intelligent production systems. To survive the fierce competition in the context of globalization, manufacturing companies have adopted the strategy of distributed manufacturing, where production facilities are located at different geographical locations. This article presents a research framework for energy efficient distributed scheduling in flow shop environment. The proposed framework has three phases, the formulation phase, the solution methodology phase, and the experimentation phase. The various inputs that need to be included in each phase are detailed with examples. This framework is proposed as an attempt to standardize the research works in the field of energy efficient distributed flow shop scheduling.

articleTitle: Deep-Learning-Based SoC Estimation for $\mathbf{LiFePO}_{4}$ Batteries Using CNN-GRU-TCN Hybrid Architecture
abstract: Accurate estimation of the state of charge (SOC) is critical for the efficient and relative operation of a battery management system (BMS) in energy storage applications. This paper presents a novel hybrid deep learning model combining convolutional neural networks (CNNs), gated recurrent units (GRUs), and temporal convolutional networks (TCNs), which combines the RNN model features and temporal dependencies of non-linear features like voltage, current, and temperature to create a relationship with SOC. The complex relationships between temporal dependencies and the monitoring signals are derived from the DL methods of lithium iron phosphate <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(\mathbf{LiFePO}_{4})$</tex> batteries. The proposed model leverages the feature extraction capabilities of CNNs, the temporal dynamics modeling of GRUs, and the long effective memory capabilities of sequence prediction strengths of TCN to enhance the accuracy and robustness of SOC estimation. We conducted experiments with <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{LiFePO}_{4}$</tex> data, taken from Influx DB, processed, and used for training and validation of models with an 80:20 ratio. Additionally, we compared the performance of our model with that of LSTM, CNN-LSTM, GRU, CNN-GRU, and CNN-GRU-LSTM. The experimental results confirm that our proposed CNN-GRU-TCN hybrid model outperforms the other models in SOC estimation in LiFePO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</inf> batteries.

articleTitle: AI-Enabled Robotic Surveillance System for Critical Infrastructure
abstract: Traditional monitoring approaches often experience blind spots and high resource utilization at such a crucial time of security. In our study, we design a small-scaled autonomous vehicle model with smart sensors that is to be equipped with an AI model in a Raspberry Pi for effective and reliable self-sustained monitoring of critical infrastructure to overcome the problems. The core AI model was specifically designed to detect in real-time anomalies such as a fire, a fight, vandalism, explosion, etc. The AI model is a modified version of an open source repository available on github named “Real-world Anomaly Detection in Surveillance Videos (pytorch) [11]”. This technology ensures speedy response time by stopping the vehicle, starting video recording, and forwarding the real-time footage to security personnel upon detecting an anomaly. This innovative solution allows for mobilization and cost-effectiveness, improving surveillance coverage, and diminished dependence on constant human oversight. Exploiting advances in artificial intelligence and robotics, the project delivers a scalable real-time monitoring system deployable into a wide range of critical infrastructure environments. This initiative represents practical application of AI towards improving public safety and building a stronger security posture in facilities that house critical infrastructure.

articleTitle: Review on Microfluidic Surface Plasmon Resonance-Based Chip for Monitoring Biomechanisms
abstract: One important analytical technique for examining biomolecular interactions in real time is surface plasmon resonance, or SPR. SPR offers label-free, non-destructive monitoring of molecule binding events by detecting changes in the refractive index at the sensor surface. SPR sensors for tracking biological functions have been integrated with microfluidic technology to boost sensitivity and throughput in biosensing applications. It begins by summarizing the fundamental concepts of SPR and how they relate to biosensing. Then, as SPR is combined with microfluidic systems, the benefits and challenges of this technology are emphasized. The rest of the paper discusses the many uses of microfluidic SPR platforms, including cell-based assays, DNA hybridization, and the study of protein-protein interactions. This review article offers a thorough examination of SPR devices based on microfluidic chips for tracking biological processes. The basic ideas of SPR and their connection to biosensing are covered first. SPR's advantages and disadvantages are then highlighted as it is used with microfluidic devices. The remainder of the study explores the wide range of applications for microfluidic SPR platforms, such as DNA hybridization, cell-based investigations, and the analysis of protein-protein interactions.

articleTitle: Proposal of Closed Loop Supply Chain Model for Medical Oxygen Cylinders
abstract: A closed-loop supply chain (CLSC) is a supply chain management system that integrates forward logistics (from production to consumer) and reverse logistics (from consumer back to the manufacturer or appropriate disposal facilities). The goal of a CLSC is to maximize the value extracted from a product by ensuring that it is reused, re manufactured, recycled, or properly disposed of after its initial use. Oxygen cylinders, critical for healthcare services, require rigorous control in their distribution, usage, and return processes to ensure uninterrupted supply and compliance with health standards. The project involves analyzing the existing supply chain of A company in Kochuveli using data obtained through discussions and identifying bottlenecks in the reverse logistics process, and developing optimised strategies for the efficient collection, inspection and redistribution of oxygen cylinders. The major problems faced by this supply chain are Logistics Complexity, Data Management and Technology, Supply Chain Disruptions, Sustainability Concerns and Economic Viability. The project plans to study the existing supply chain and do comprehensive analysis of current supply chain operations, identification of potential recovery strategies, and the design of an optimized CLSC model. The various tools that can be used to solve the problems are Vehicle routing, Facility layout, Optimised path layout, Transportation analysis and Linear programming,ant colony optimization algorithm and other mathematical theorems. The expected outcomes are supposed to be increased efficiency and cost savings, enhanced sustainability, data driven decision making,optimized route and fleet management.

articleTitle: Enhancing Healthcare Service Quality: An Integrated Approach Using SERVQUAL, Patient Journey Analysis, and AI-Driven Solutions
abstract: This study evaluates service quality in the outpatient department of a healthcare facility using the SERVQUAL model, complemented by emotional and journey mapping techniques. The research aims to identify critical service gaps and provide evidence-based recommendations for improving patientsatisfaction and operational efficiency. A case study was conducted in a leading private hospital in South India, focusing onareas for potential improvement. A sample of 200 patients, equally divided between chemotherapy and review patients, was surveyed using an adopted SERVQUAL questionnaire [22]. Thequestionnaire assessed five dimensions: tangibility, reliability, responsiveness, assurance, and empathy. The study revealed significant gaps in responsiveness and empathy, indicating areas requiring immediate attention. Identified issues include ineffective communication, staff shortages, and inefficient patient scheduling. To address these gaps, this study proposes a multi-faceted approach to address healthcare service quality gaps, combining technological solutions and human-centred strategies. The interventions include AI-powered scheduling, process automation, AI-enhanced communication, RFID-enabled asset management, and integrated billing systems. This research contributes to the growing body of knowledge on healthcare service quality and offers practical solutions for healthcare providers to enhance patient experiences and operational efficiencies.

articleTitle: Paddy Leaf Disease Identification and Automated Remedial Initiation using Pesticide Sprayer
abstract: Rice is one of the most important staple crops in the world, providing food for billions of people. However, several illnesses, such as paddy leaf diseases, which can drastically lower crop yields and quality, frequently pose a threat to rice production. Our goal is to create a system that can automatically detect diseases in paddy leaves and use a pesticide sprayer to start corrective action. The pesticide sprayer is triggered to apply the appropriate treatment by the system, which uses image processing techniques to determine the type and severity of the disease. The proposed model detects paddy leaf diseases and provide necessary pesticide for the treatment of these diseases through an automated pesticide sprayer system. With this we could drastically lower the workload and expenses related to manual disease identification and treatment, the system is made to be economical, effective, and user-friendly. In addition to lowering the time and expense involved in diagnosing and treating diseases, the system is anticipated to increase treatment efficacy and precision. By limiting the quantity of pesticide used and lowering the possibility of overuse or misuse, the system is also anticipated to lessen the negative effects of pesticide use on the environment. All things considered, this project is a significant step toward the creation of creative and sustainable solutions to the problems the agriculture sector faces.

articleTitle: ResoBlend: A Hybrid Approach for Image Quality Enhancement
abstract: The Resoblend project aims to revolutionize image enhancement by addressing the critical need for improved image quality in the face of limited availability of effective enhancement techniques. In today's data-driven world, the quality of images plays a pivotal role in various fields, from medical diagnostics to satellite imaging. However, low-exposure and low-resolution images often pose significant challenges, compromising the accuracy and reliability of visual data interpretation. Existing enhancement techniques have limitations in preserving image details and achieving optimal exposure balance, further exacerbating the problem. To tackle these challenges, the Resoblend project proposes a novel approach that combines advanced image fusion and super-resolution techniques. By leveraging cutting-edge deep learning models and machine learning techniques, Resoblend offers a comprehensive solution to enhance image quality, preserve critical details, and achieve optimal exposure balance. Through rigorous evaluation and validation using established performance metrics, Resoblend demonstrates its effectiveness and reliability in improving image quality and fidelity. Moreover, the project explores a wide range of potential applications, spanning from medical imaging to remote sensing and industrial imaging, highlighting its versatility and utility in real-world scenarios.

articleTitle: Evolving Perspectives in Nuclear Atypia Scoring: From Traditional Methods to Modern Insights
abstract: Early breast cancer detection greatly improves treatment success and survival rates, allowing for less invasive treatments and better quality of life. Screening and diagnostic methods are essential for identifying cancer in its early stages, leading to timely interventions. Nuclear atypia scoring is crucial for diagnosis and survival, helping detect malignant cell changes and guide treatment. This review evaluates recent advancements, including deep learning techniques, and addresses the advancement and challenges in nuclear atypia assessment. It explores traditional methods, cutting-edge technologies, inter-observer variability, and data integration, emphasizing the evolving role of accurate scoring in enhancing patient care and understanding breast cancer progression.

articleTitle: Designing Assistive Smart Glasses for Sudden Vision Loss: Empowering the Elderly and Technology-Averse Users
abstract: Visually impaired individuals, particularly those who have recently lost their sight or struggle to adapt to new technology, face significant challenges in navigating their environment. Conventional aids mostly have no real-time feedback and lack complete spatial awareness, leading to minimal independence and very high risks in unknown environments. To address these challenges, we propose “SmartSight”, an AI-powered wearable device designed to meet diverse needs. SmartVision merges advanced computer vision, Visual SLAM, and deep learning into one real-time assistance system. It features environmental analysis, indoor/outdoor navigation, face detection, social media connectivity, and OCR for reading, with an easy-to-use interface. By leveraging cutting-edge embedded systems and sensor fusion, SmartSight provides immediate, accurate feedback to enhance spatial awareness, independence and safety. This comprehensive solution is designed to be the ultimate assistive tool, which aims at making visually impaired users navigate with full confidence, and independence while bridging the gap between their previous experiences and current challenges.

articleTitle: Advanced DC Voltage Regulator for Photovoltaic Systems
abstract: The increasing prominence of solar energy in addressing global energy demands underscores the critical role played by photovoltaic (PV) modules. However, the inherent challenges associated with solar irradiance and temperature fluctuations contribute to the relatively low efficiency of traditional PV modules. Recognizing this limitation, the introduction of high-efficiency DC-DC converters, such as the KY converter, emerges as a pivotal advancement tailored specifically to enhance the performance of PV modules. The KY converter distinguishes itself through characteristics such as small output voltage ripples and a rapid transient response, differentiating it from conventional boost converters. Its design is meticulously optimized to address the variability in environmental conditions, ensuring the extraction of maximum power from PV panels. A key focus lies in minimizing energy losses during the conversion process, a crucial aspect for overall efficiency improvement. What sets the KY converter apart is not only its technical capabilities but also the incorporation of innovative control algorithms and design features. These elements collectively contribute to achieving outstanding efficiency, robustness, and reliability in the operation of the converter. This marks a significant advancement in the ongoing pursuit of more sustainable and efficient solar energy generation technologies. In essence, the KY converter represents a crucial component in the broader strategy to enhance the efficiency of solar energy systems. By addressing the limitations of traditional PV modules and mitigating energy losses through advanced design and control mechanisms, this converter plays a vital role in pushing the boundaries of what is achievable in the quest for a cleaner and more sustainable energy future.

articleTitle: Context-Driven Chatbot Development: Leveraging Zephyr-7b with RAG for Improved Response Accuracy
abstract: In recent years, the demand for AI-driven conversational agents has increased significantly across various industries. Traditional generative models, while capable of producing human-like responses, often struggle with factual accuracy and context retention. Retrieval Augmented Generation (RAG) presents a novel approach to enhance the performance of AI chatbots by combining the strengths of both retrieval-based and generative models. The paper focuses on the development of an AI-driven chatbot using a RAG framework, integrating the Zephyr-7b model, to serve the needs of the ICT Academy of Kerala (ICTAK). The chatbot is engineered to deliver precise and contextually relevant responses to user queries by integrating advanced language models with structured data extracted from the ICTAK website. The data, which was meticulously scraped and processed, ensures that the chatbot's knowledge base remains current and accurately reflects the ICTAK's services and operations. A critical challenge addressed by this work is the issue of hallucinations in large language models (LLMs), where models may generate seemingly plausible yet incorrect or irrelevant information. To counteract this, the paper employs various chunking methods that enhance the chatbot's capability to retrieve and generate accurate responses. This AI Chatbot incorporates cutting-edge techniques in natural language processing, including document retrieval, context compression, and re-ranking. This multi-faceted approach ensures that the chatbot not only provides accurate responses but also delivers them in a contextually relevant manner.

articleTitle: Comprehensive Review on Deep Compressive Sensing Algorithms for Image Reconstruction
abstract: Image reconstruction is a fundamental problem in various fields, and deep learning has emerged as a powerful tool for achieving state-of-the-art results. This paper presents a comprehensive review of deep-learning algorithms for image reconstruction. We analyse and compare the performance of these algorithms highlighting their strengths and limitations. Furthermore, this review aims to illuminate promising research directions and inspire future innovation in deep learning-based CS. We delve into interpretability challenges, often encountered in complex deep learning models, and their implications for image reconstruction. Additionally, we address the issues of computational complexity, parameter optimisation, and the need for efficient parameter usage, particularly in resource-constrained settings. The review concludes by outlining promising future research directions, emphasizing the development of more interpretable, computationally efficient, and data-efficient deep learning algorithms for image reconstruction.

articleTitle: Advanced Metering Infrastructure Survey on Security: Vulnerabilities, Attacks, and Countermeasures for a 5kW PV Microgrid
abstract: The growing digitalization of power systems has required the need of Smart Grids (SGs), it merges traditional energy distribution framework with communication technology. A central feature of these grids is Advanced Metering Infrastructure (AMI), It enables bidirectional communication between consumers and energy providers. It is one of the main components of a smart grid. It offers real time overview of electricity usage which improves operational efficiency and optimizes power demand management. As there is an increased dependency of AMI system which rely on interconnected network and cloud-based data handling they introduce new security challenges. The potential issues include unauthorized breaches, data manipulation, and service interruptions all threaten the dependability of smart grid operations. This study examines vulnerabilities at multiple levels of AMI system-hardware, data and communication-and surveys on recent SGs, security measures and intrusion detection systems (IDS). It will focus on attack, approach to mitigate and provide counter measures in the context of a 5kW solar power microgrid. The security considerations and best practices identified here were designed and implemented in the main system.

articleTitle: Enhancing Prediabetes Prediction Using Hybrid CNNs and SMOTE for Data Imbalance
abstract: Prediabetes, a condition characterized by elevated blood glucose levels, is a critical precursor to Type II diabetes. Early detection of prediabetes can significantly reduce the risk of progression to full-blown diabetes, as well as associated complications. However, the imbalance in medical datasets poses a challenge to accurate prediction, often leading to the underper-formance of conventional machine learning models. In this study, we propose a hybrid Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) model combined with the Synthetic Minority Over-sampling Technique (SMOTE) to enhance the prediction of prediabetes. By addressing the class imbalance problem, our approach improves the predictive accuracy for the prediabetic class, which is typically underrepresented in datasets. The hybrid CNN model is evaluated against traditional machine learning techniques, such as logistic regression, decision trees, support vector machine (SVM) and artificial neural network (ANN), demonstrating superior performance in terms of precision, recall, and overall accuracy. Our results indicate that integrating SMOTE with deep learning models offers a robust solution for enhancing the early detection of prediabetes, providing healthcare practitioners with a valuable tool for implementing timely preventive interventions.

articleTitle: Multimodal Fusion of Speech and Action Recognition for IoT Device
abstract: Developments in deep learning techniques have opened up novel possibilities in the multimodal data fusion field. However, there is a significant gap in the capability of deep learning algorithms to handle multimodal data in real time across various modalities. This work aims to develop a model that integrates deep learning, computer vision, and speech recognition methods to accurately interpret human commands conveyed through gestures and voice in real time. The gesture identification problem was modelled using the Long-Short Term Memory (LSTM) networks. This model was trained on key points that are extracted from landmarks recognized using the MediaPipe architecture. Similarly, Speech recognition utilises the Short-term Fourier transform to generate a spectrogram, which is then inputted into Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) to parallelly analyze and recognize spoken commands from audio recordings. The models are combined utilizing a late fusion strategy to make a united decision. The proposed methodology achieved above 95 % accuracy for both speech and gesture recognition modal.

articleTitle: FedCosA: Optimised Federated Learning Model Using Cosine Annealing
abstract: The Federated Learning paradigm allows multiple devices or nodes to contribute to model training without sharing raw data, ensuring that sensitive information remains on the client side while still benefiting from collective learning. However, FL suffers several problems, including slow convergence, overfitting, and communication cost, particularly in Non-Independent and Identically Distributed (Non-IID) data settings. To solve these concerns, we offer an improved Federated Averaging (FedAvg) method that includes the Adam optimizer, cosine annealing learning rate scheduler, and weight decay (L2 regularisation). The Adam optimizer generates adaptive learning rates, but the cosine annealing schedule refines the learning rate over time for greater stability. Weight decay reduces overfitting by penalizing big model parameters. Furthermore, picking a subset of customers in each cycle lowers communication costs. Experimental findings on the MNIST dataset show that our strategy outperforms existing FL algorithms like FedAvg, FedSGD, FedNova, and FedSAM in test accuracy and loss minimization while significantly lowering communication load and training time. These enhancements make the suggested approach more effective and scalable for FL across several settings.

articleTitle: Advancing Gastrointestinal Tract Cancer Treatment: A Comparative Study of State-of-the-Art Deep Learning Models for MRI Segmentation
abstract: This paper investigates the performance of state-of-the-art deep learning models for segmenting the gastrointestinal (GI) tract in Magnetic Resonance Imaging (MRI) images, a critical step in radiotherapy planning for GI tract cancers. Manual segmentation of the GI tract is time-consuming, error-prone, and complicated by anatomical complexity and patient movement. To automate this process, we explore various deep learning techniques for their potential to provide accurate and efficient segmentation. Specifically, this study compares Feature Pyramid Networks (FPN), LinkNet, Pyramid Scene Parsing Networks (PSPNet), and traditional U-Net architectures and their variants. Using the publicly available UW Madison GI Tract Image Segmentation dataset, which includes 38,496 MRI scans with corresponding RLE-encoded masks, we evaluate architectures such as U-Net with different encoders (EfficientNetB1, MobileNetV2, and ResNet50), U-Net++ with EfficientNetB1, PSP-Net (EfficientNetB1 and ResNet34), FPN (EfficientNetB0 and EfficientNetB1) and LinkNet with EfficientNetB1. The models were trained using a standardized protocol over 30 epochs, with performance assessed through the Dice and Jaccard/IoU coefficients. Results indicate that the models achieved Dice scores ranging from 0.86 to 0.89, with no single model consistently out-performing the others. However, U-Net variations with residual connections demonstrated the most robust performance overall. This study provides valuable insights into the application of deep learning for medical image segmentation. It lays the groundwork for further research to enhance segmentation accuracy in GI cancer treatment, ultimately contributing to improved patient care and expedited treatment planning.

articleTitle: Credit Card Fraud Detection using Machine Learning Methods
abstract: As per the data transactions are made online, credit card fraud continues to be a growing problem. We present a new real-time, live detection approach for fraud in research. We cluster cardholders according to their transaction patterns and use a supervised machine learning approach to identify fraudulent behavior (card issuer wary of fraud). It is a massive problem in the financial industry and one of its biggest enemies, leading to major monetary losses with which millions or even billions can be achieved frontally. The model is iteratively updated by a feedback loop to adapt baffle responses against changing fraudster tactics. In this paper, we are using a logistic regression model in order to detect credit card frauds via machine learning. In this study, real-world credit card transactions with a great class imbalance (i.e. the number of frauds is far lower than that for normal activities) are used as a training data set. This is handled by steps like data preprocessing, normalization, encoding and sampling techniques intended to make the model robust: (i. e., more accurate). EDA — Since we can conduct our EDA on this dataset to see the overall pattern, which will be valuable in identifying what features are most important for fraudulent behavior. This data is then broken down into a training dataset and testing datasets to assess the predictions made by our model.

articleTitle: Federated Clustering Defense: Mitigating Data Exposure in Collaborative Learning
abstract: The development of intelligent industrial applications is being driven globally by advancements in the next generation of Internet of Things (IoT) technologies. At the same time, artificial intelligence (AI) technologies like machine learning and deep learning are becoming more widely used. Conventional machine learning models primarily rely on large data sets. However, the vast data sets generated by network-edge devices are expensive, inefficient to acquire and handle, and they pose major privacy hazards. Federated learning (FL) is a novel paradigm for statistical model training on distributed edge networks that allows data to take part in the training of federated models without being localized. Traditional machine learning issues with low data usage, data privacy, and information security brought on by data isolation can be resolved with this method. We propose a novel Federated Clustering with Differential Privacy (FedCDP) algorithm designed to efficiently model user behavior in an unsupervised manner. This algorithm focuses on optimizing computation and storage requirements while minimizing data leakage through robust differential privacy mechanisms.

articleTitle: Regulating Software as Medical Device (SaMD): A Comprehensive Overview of The International Medical Device Regulators Forum (IMDRF) Framework and Gap Analysis of Indian Medical Devices Rules, 2017
abstract: The rapid advancement of digital health technologies has led to the increasing importance of Software as Medical Device (SaMD) in modern healthcare. This paper examines the regulatory landscape for SaMD, with a specific focus on the International Medical Device Regulators Forum (IMDRF) framework. The IMDRF's risk-based classification system is explored in detail, highlighting its importance in determining regulatory requirements. We discuss the lifecycle requirements for SaMD, encompassing the design, development, verification, and validation phases, as well as the importance of continuous post-market surveillance. The clinical evaluation of SaMD, a critical component of ensuring safety and efficacy, is also analyzed, with emphasis on the unique challenges posed by SaMDs. This paper aims to provide a comprehensive overview of the IMDRF framework's approach to SaMD regulation and offers insights into the current gaps in the Indian Medical Devices Rules, 2017 (IMDR) related to SaMD regulations.

articleTitle: Algebraic Topology for Data-Driven Artifact Removal Post-Video Stabilization of Indoor Videos Captured by Mobile Robots: Theory, Algorithm and Experiments
abstract: Video stabilization is the process of removing unwanted shaky motion from a video sequence. Often, it can be observed that the frames in the video obtained after stabilization (stabilized video) have some unknown unintended artifacts associated with it, resulting in degradation of its quality. This poses a challenge in inferring visual information from a stabilized video. In this work, we present a novel data-driven approach to enhance the quality of stabilized video by gaining insights into the indoor part of the natural image manifold using homological algebra. The enhancement is achieved by projecting the stabilized video frames onto an approximated thickened triangulated version of the manifold underlying an indoor image dataset, which we refer to as the indoor image manifold. This manifold can be thought of as an open subset of the natural image manifold, which is the part over which the indoor images are dense. The manifold is reconstructed using the lower bounds on the rank of Homology groups of the indoor image manifold. The lower bounds are derived using the functorial properties of classical singular homology. Our approach has been found to increase video stabilization quality assessment (VSQA) scores for certain classes of indoor stabilized videos from datasets.

articleTitle: Sentiment Classification for Depression Detection: Integrating Capsule Networks with CNNs on Review Data
abstract: This research is focused on the analysis of how Capsule Networks should be combined with Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) for improving the sentiment classification with the target of depression detection based on the data offered by the reviews. Other methodologies of analysing the sentiment of a phrase may encounter disability in the process of analysing texts in natural language following depression since they do not analyse the text deeply enough to consider the context. The proposed method intends to enhance accuracy and resistance when compared to state-of-the-art techniques by combining the attributes of Capsule Networks, that effectively maintain the spatial hierarchy and the connections within the data, with CNNs’ feature extraction ability. The proposed hybrid model helps overcome disadvantages of the plain sentiment analysis because it identifies intricate patterns and dependencies in the review data and enhances the depressive sentiments’ detection. This paper assesses the propriety of the integrated Capsule-CNN through an evaluation on review datasets in relation to its ability in the successful differentiate between depressive and non-depressive sentiments. The findings reveal a considerable increase in method accuracy and present a leap of progress in the field of automatic depression detection, which in turn helps to develop more accurate and efficient tools for monitoring patients’ mental status.

articleTitle: POWER VORTEX - Smart Energy Forecasting and Management with IoT and Machine Learning
abstract: Power Vortex is an innovative smart power consumption management system designed to replace traditional switchboards with intelligent alternatives. This advanced solution connects various devices, accurately measures their power consumption, and sends the data to a centralized server for analysis. Through a user-friendly mobile app, equipped with cutting-edge machine learning algorithms like LSTM, RNN, and analytics, consumers gain access to real-time energy usage insights, personalized usage reports, and actionable recommendations. In this project, we present the comprehensive design, development, and testing of Power Vortex, highlighting its pivotal role in effectively managing power consumption. Beyond traditional energy management systems, our device harnesses the power of machine learning to predict and provide valuable recommendations to users based on their energy use patterns, preferences, and external factors. These personalized recommendations empower users to make informed decisions, optimize their energy consumption, and reduce costs. Power Vortex demonstrates tangible benefits in terms of both financial savings and environmental impact. By integrating a smart switchboard to connect and monitor devices, it delivers precise and real-time energy consumption data to users. This data-driven approach not only fosters efficient resource utilization, but also supports the larger goal of environmental sustainability. Power Vortex is poised to revolutionize energy management practices, offering a more sustainable future by enabling individuals and organizations to reduce their carbon footprint and create a positive impact on the environment.

articleTitle: Schematic Review on the Application of Blockchain and IoT Integration with Sentiment Analysis in Supply Chain Management
abstract: This schematic review presents a comprehensive comparative analysis of the integration of blockchain technology, sentiment analysis, and IoT devices within the domain of supply chain management. By exploring the intersection of these cutting-edge paradigms, the study investigates their collective impact on augmenting transparency, traceability, and operational efficiency across a variety of supply chain ecosystems. Synthesizing insights from diverse industries, the review systematically assesses the implementation, advantages, and challenges associated with lever-aging blockchain for secure data exchange, sentiment analysis for real-time insights, and IoT devices for data acquisition to bolster food traceability systems within dynamic supply chain settings. Additionally, the review examines the adaptability, scalability, and interpretability of these technologies, providing valuable insights into their synergistic potential and limitations within the intricate landscape of supply chain operations. With a focus on the significance of data integrity, trust mechanisms, and sentiment-driven decision-making, this abstract serves as an indispensable guide for practitioners, researchers, and stakeholders navigating the strategic integration of blockchain, sentiment analysis, and IoT devices in contemporary supply chain frameworks.

articleTitle: Human Exclusive Alerts in CCTV Surveillance Using Computer Vision
abstract: This paper outlines a proposed approach to enhance modern surveillance systems by addressing the challenges posed by the excessive data generated by extensive CCTV camera networks. The proliferation of surveillance footage often results in inefficiencies, primarily due to false alarms triggered by non-human movements such as animals or environmental factors. The proposed system aims to tackle this issue by integrating advanced computer vision technologies with state-of-the-art deep learning algorithms, designed to accurately identify human presence and thereby significantly reduce irrelevant alerts Our intended solution involves the adoption of the latest YOLO (You Only Look Once) object detection model, YOLOv8, which is renowned for its efficiency and accuracy in real-time object recognition. We plan to combine this with OpenCV, a robust tool for image processing and computer vision tasks, to enhance our system's capability to process and analyze video data effectively. Furthermore, we aim to utilize the COCO dataset, a comprehensive object detection, segmentation, and captioning dataset, to train our deep learning algorithms. This training will equip our system to differentiate effectively between human and non-human elements by famil-iarizing it with a wide range of human poses and activities. The methodology we propose is currently undergoing rigorous validation and extensive real-world testing. We anticipate that these efforts will demonstrate the effectiveness of our approach in minimizing false alarms and maximizing the accuracy of human detection across various surveillance environments. By refining alert precision, our approach aims to enhance security measures, allowing surveillance operators to concentrate more on genuine human-related incidents. The research not only seeks to improve the operational efficiency of surveillance systems but also aims to contribute to the broader field of security technology by demonstrating potential applications of cutting-edge artificial intelligence in real-world scenarios

articleTitle: Emotion Detection From Speech for Improved Communication Accessibility
abstract: This paper aims to develop a robust emotion recognition system that accurately classifies emotions from speech, with potential applications in accessibility technologies, gauging mental health, and interactions among users and computers. The primary objective is to devise a model that is adept at recognizing the elementary emotions-angry, disgust, fear, happy, neutral, sad, and surprise-using audio features extracted from speech datasets. Through the exploitation of the diversity of datasets available, that include, TESS, RAVDESS, and CREMA-D and SAVEE, we ensure that the model is highly generalizable across the different variations of speakers, emotional intensities, and recording environments. We preprocess the data by unifying emotion labels, standardizing formats, and extracting prosodic features like Mel-Frequency Cepstral Coefficients (MFCCs). After preparing the data, we apply machine learning techniques to capture spatial and temporal features based on the voice signals. The model is trained and evaluated on an 80/20 split, ensuring it is tested on a wide variety of unseen data. The model reaches an accuracy rate of 95%, with balanced precision, recall, and F1-scores across all emotion categories. It exhibits strong performance in categorizing emotional states from speech. Its potential is considerable in practical scenarios, especially in improving accessibility for the deaf and hard-of-hearing, enriching user experiences using AI-driven systems, and even in assistance with diagnostics related to mental health.

articleTitle: A Brief Study on Deepfake Detection and Prevention Approaches
abstract: Images, movies, and sounds produced using artificial intelligence (AI) technologies that depict events or things that do not exist in reality are known as Deepfakes. Large volumes of labeled training data are needed for deep learning models, which are frequently employed in AI-based Deepfake detection, to learn meaningful representations of real and modified material. The expanding complexity of AI-generated material has raised concerns about Deepfake prevention. The prevention of Deepfake technology abuse necessitates a multifaceted strategy that includes social, legal, and technological safeguards. In this paper describes a guideline for Deepfake detection and prevention methods, its supporting tools and specifies various datasets to solving different modalities.

articleTitle: Seizures Prediction using Heart Rate Variability in ECG Signal
abstract: An exploratory study was suggested to assess the efficacy of an automatic model, and this model helps to identify heart rate (HR) changes in individuals with severe epilepsy during seizures. Heart rate (HR) is one of the automatic body functions that can alter as a result of epileptic seizures. Mainly, the method proposed in the study was used to check disruptions in the heart signal, called movement artifacts, on the ECG. These disruptions in the heart signal make it harder to detect R-peaks, which are the main spikes in the ECG, and can also reduce the accuracy of seizure detection algorithms as well. Importantly, the Artefacts Detection Algorithm introduced a new feature, which uses Principal Component Analysis (PCA) to analyze electrocardiogram (ECG) signals and can be used to describe the changes within ECG data as well. The new feature is highly focused to detect seizures by analyzing changes in the morphological characteristics (shape and structure) of the electrocardiogram signal, especially those in the QRS complex, which can indicate seizure activity. One type of machine learning model used to distinguish between normal and abnormal ECG signals is the Support Vector Machine (SVM). The clustering algorithm ‘K-means’ is used to identify seizures. The normal and abnormal signals can be easily differentiated by the system. SVM, along with k-means algorithms are used to detect seizures in a more accurate manner.

articleTitle: Harnessing Wi-Fi CSI for Enhanced Human Activity Recognition: A Feature-Driven Approach
abstract: Wi-Fi routers are ubiquitous in modern households, offering the capability to estimate Wi-Fi channel state information (CSI), which can be harnessed to sense the surrounding environment. CSI captures intricate signal variations resulting from human movement, such as amplitude, phase, and Time of Flight (ToF). This paper proposes a Human Activity Recognition (HAR) method based on a dataset of CSI features. The features were extracted across multiple dimensions, including time-domain, frequency-domain, statistical, temporal, and spatial characteristics. Feature selection techniques, such as correlation analysis, were employed to reduce data dimensionality. Machine learning models were trained on the refined feature set for indoor environments in line-of-sight (LOS) and non-line-of-sight (NLOS) scenarios. Our method significantly outperformed the raw Wi-Fi CSI dataset-based approach in HAR classification accuracy. The results demonstrate the effectiveness of various classifiers in HAR using Wi-Fi CSI feature data. This study provides critical insights into the application of feature extraction and selection techniques for precise activity recognition, with potential applications in healthcare, security, and human-computer interaction.
